bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第201卷卷第二百一

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 201, Volume the Two Hundred and First.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 201.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十七】起玄勣閹茂八月，盡上章困敦，凡八年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 17] From the eighth month of the Xuanji year through the Kun Dun month of the Shangzhang year—in all eight years and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 17] The span runs from the eighth month of the Xuanji cycle year through the Kun Dun month of the Shangzhang cycle year—eight years and a fraction in all.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，以許敬宗為太子少師、同東西台三品、知西台事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, Xu Jingzong was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices, and charged with Western Office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, Xu Jingzong was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices, with charge of Western Office business.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅，初令八品、九品衣碧。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuyin, for the first time eighth- and ninth-rank officials were ordered to wear green.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuyin, officials of the eighth and ninth ranks were for the first time required to wear green robes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，上幸驪山溫湯，太子監國；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li; the crown prince supervised the state;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li while the crown prince oversaw the government;

sentences.zh: 丁未，還宮。

translations.literal: on dingwei he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on dingwei he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，西台侍郎陝人上官儀同東西台三品。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Shangguan Yi of Shaan, Vice Director of the Western Office, was made Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Shangguan Yi of Shaan, Vice Director of the Western Office, was appointed Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔以四年正月有事於泰山，仍以來年二月幸東都。

translations.literal: On guichou, an edict ordered that in the first month of the fourth year there be rites at Mount Tai, and that in the second month of the following year the emperor should visit the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, an edict set rites at Mount Tai for the first month of the fourth year and a visit to the Eastern Capital for the second month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 左相許圉師之子奉輦直長自然，遊獵犯人田，田主怒，自然以鳴鏑射之。

translations.literal: The son of Left Chancellor Xu Yushi, Ziran, a Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, while hunting trespassed on a farmer's field; the farmer grew angry, and Ziran shot at him with a whistling arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Ziran, son of Left Chancellor Xu Yushi and a Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, trespassed on a farmer's land while hunting; when the farmer protested, Ziran shot at him with a whistling arrow.

sentences.zh: 圉師杖自然一百而不以聞。

translations.literal: Yushi had Ziran beaten one hundred strokes but did not report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yushi had Ziran flogged a hundred strokes but never reported the incident to the throne.

sentences.zh: 田主詣司憲訟之，司憲大夫楊德裔不為治。

translations.literal: The farmer went to the Office of the Censor to sue; Censor-in-Chief Yang Deyi would not hear the case.
translations.idiomatic: The farmer brought suit before the Office of the Censor, but Censor-in-Chief Yang Deyi refused to take up the case.

sentences.zh: 西台舍人袁公瑜遣人易姓名上封事告之，上曰：「圉師為宰相，侵陵百姓，匿而不言，豈非作威作福！」

translations.literal: Western Office Attendant Yuan Gongyu sent someone to submit a sealed memorial under a changed name reporting this; the emperor said, "Yushi is a chancellor who bullies the people and conceals wrongdoing without reporting it—is this not making might and making blessings for himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gongyu, an attendant of the Western Office, had someone submit a sealed memorial under a false name; the emperor said, "As chancellor, Yushi bullies the people and hides the affair without reporting it—is that not the arrogance of one who makes his own might and fortune?"

sentences.zh: 圉師謝曰：「臣備位樞軸，以直道事陛下，不能悉允眾心，故為人所攻訐。

translations.literal: Yushi apologized, saying, "Your servant holds a place at the pivot of government and serves Your Majesty by the straight path; I cannot wholly satisfy every heart, and so I am attacked and impeached by others.
translations.idiomatic: Yushi apologized: "I hold office at the heart of government and serve Your Majesty with integrity; I cannot please everyone, and so I am slandered.

sentences.zh: 至於作威福者，或手握強兵，或身居重鎮；

translations.literal: As for those who make might and blessings for themselves, some grasp strong armies in their hands, or themselves hold heavy border commands;
translations.idiomatic: Those who truly lord it over others either command great armies or hold key frontier posts;

sentences.zh: 臣以文吏，奉事聖明，惟知閉門自守，何敢作威福！」

translations.literal: your servant is a civil official who serves a sage and enlightened ruler; I know only to shut my door and keep myself in check—how would I dare to make might and blessings for myself!"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a civil clerk serving a sage sovereign; I know nothing but to keep my door shut and mind my own affairs—how could I play the tyrant!"

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「汝恨無兵邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger, "Do you resent that you have no troops!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared up: "So you regret that you have no army!"

sentences.zh: 許敬宗曰：「人臣如此，罪不容誅。」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong said, "A subject who speaks thus—his crime admits no punishment short of death."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong said, "A minister who speaks like this deserves death beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 遽令引出。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered led out.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately ordered out of court.

sentences.zh: 詔特免官。

translations.literal: An edict specially stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，立皇子旭輪為殷王。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the imperial son Xulun was established as Prince of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the emperor's son Xulun was created Prince of Yin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊申，詔以方討高麗、百濟，河北之民，勞於征役，其封泰山、幸東都並停。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wushen, an edict said that because campaigns were underway against Goguryeo and Baekje and the people of Hebei were worn out by corvée and levies, the feng at Mount Tai and the visit to the Eastern Capital were both suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen, an edict noted that with campaigns against Goguryeo and Baekje still in progress and the people of Hebei exhausted by levies; both the Mount Tai feng rites and the visit to the Eastern Capital were suspended.

sentences.zh: 風海道總管蘇海政受詔討龜茲，敕興昔亡、繼往絕二可汗發兵與之俱。

translations.literal: Fenghai Circuit Commander Su Haizheng received orders to attack Kucha and was instructed that the two khans Xingxiwang and Jiwangjue should raise troops and go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Haizheng, commander of the Fenghai route, was ordered to campaign against Kucha; the khans Xingxiwang and Jiwangjue were commanded to mobilize and join him.

sentences.zh: 至興昔亡之境，繼往絕素與興昔亡有怨，密謂海政曰：「彌射謀反，請誅之。」

translations.literal: When they reached Xingxiwang's territory, Jiwangjue, who had long borne a grudge against Xingxiwang, secretly told Haizheng, "Mishe is plotting rebellion—please execute him."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Xingxiwang's territory, Jiwangjue—who had long been at odds with him—privately told Haizheng, "Mishe is plotting revolt; put him to death."

sentences.zh: 時海政兵才數千，集軍吏謀曰：「彌射若反，我輩無□類，不如先事誅之。」

translations.literal: At that time Haizheng had only a few thousand troops; he gathered his officers and said, "If Mishe rebels, none of us will survive—we had better strike first and kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Haizheng had only a few thousand men; he called his officers together and said, "If Mishe turns on us, none of us will live—we should kill him first."

sentences.zh: 乃矯稱敕，令大總管繼帛數萬段賜可汗及諸酋長，興昔亡帥其徒受賜，海政悉收斬之。

translations.literal: He then forged an imperial order in the name of the Grand Commander, granting tens of thousands of bolts of silk to the khan and the various chieftains; Xingxiwang led his followers to receive the gifts, and Haizheng seized and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an imperial order in the Grand Commander's name, offering tens of thousands of bolts of silk to the khan and the chiefs; when Xingxiwang brought his men forward to receive them, Haizheng seized and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 其鼠尼施、拔塞干兩部亡走，海政與繼往絕追討，平之。

translations.literal: The two tribes Shunishi and Basagan fled; Haizheng and Jiwangjue pursued and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunishi and Basagan tribes fled; Haizheng and Jiwangjue pursued them and brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 軍還，至疏勒南，弓月部復引吐蕃之眾來，欲與唐兵戰；

translations.literal: On the army's return, south of Shule, the Gongyue tribe again brought Tibetan forces to fight the Tang army;
translations.idiomatic: On the march home, south of Shule, the Gongyue tribe again led Tibetan troops against the Tang forces;

sentences.zh: 海政以師老不敢戰，以軍資賂吐蕃，約和而還。

translations.literal: Haizheng, finding his troops weary, dared not give battle; he bribed the Tibetans with military stores, made peace, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Haizheng's troops were exhausted and he dared not fight; he bought off the Tibetans with army supplies, made peace, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由是諸部落皆以興昔亡為冤，各有離心。

translations.literal: From this the various tribes all regarded Xingxiwang as wronged and each grew disaffected.
translations.idiomatic: After this the tribes all felt Xingxiwang had been wronged, and their loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 繼往絕尋卒，十姓無主，有阿史那都支及李遮匐收其餘眾附於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Jiwangjue soon died; the Ten Surnames were left without a leader, and Ashina Duzhi and Li Zhefu gathered the remaining followers and attached themselves to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwangjue soon died; with no leader over the Ten Surnames, Ashina Duzhi and Li Zhefu rallied the survivors and submitted to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 是歲，西突厥寇庭州，刺史來濟將兵拒之，謂其眾曰：「吾久當死，幸蒙存全以至今日，當以身報國！」

translations.literal: That year the Western Turks raided Ting Prefecture; Prefect Lai Ji led troops to resist them and told his men, "Long ago I ought to have died; by good fortune I was spared to live until today—I must repay the state with my body!"
translations.idiomatic: That year the Western Turks attacked Ting Prefecture; Prefect Lai Ji led the defense and told his men, "I should have died long ago; only grace spared me until now—I will repay the realm with my life!"

sentences.zh: 遂不釋甲冑，赴敵而死。

translations.literal: He then, without removing armor, rushed the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: Without doffing his armor, he charged the enemy and was killed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，左武衛將軍鄭仁泰討鐵勒叛者餘種，悉平之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zuo Wuwei General Zheng Rentai campaigned against the remaining Tiele rebels and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, General Zheng Rentai of the Left Wuwei Guard campaigned against the remaining Tiele rebels and subdued them all.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以李義府為右相，仍知選事。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Li Yifu was appointed Right Chancellor and continued to oversee selection of officials.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Li Yifu was made Right Chancellor and kept charge of official appointments.

sentences.zh: 二月，徙燕然都護府於回紇，更名瀚海都護；

translations.literal: In the second month, the Yanran Protectorate was moved to the Uyghurs and renamed the Hanhai Protectorate;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Yanran Protectorate was moved to Uyghur territory and renamed the Hanhai Protectorate;

sentences.zh: 徙故瀚海都護於雲中古城，更名雲中都護。

translations.literal: the former Hanhai Protectorate was moved to the old city of Yunzhong and renamed the Yunzhong Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: the former Hanhai Protectorate was relocated to the old city of Yunzhong and renamed the Yunzhong Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 以磧為境，磧北州府皆隸瀚海，磧南隸雲中。

translations.literal: The desert was taken as the boundary: prefectures and protectorates north of the desert all belonged to Hanhai, those south to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The desert marked the boundary: all prefectures north of it fell under Hanhai, those south under Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 三月，許圉師再貶虔州刺史，楊德裔以阿黨流庭州，圉師子文思、自然並免官。

translations.literal: In the third month, Xu Yushi was again demoted to prefect of Qian; Yang Deyi was exiled to Ting Prefecture for factionalism; Yushi's sons Wensi and Ziran were both stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Xu Yushi was demoted again to prefect of Qian; Yang Deyi was exiled to Ting for factional conduct; Yushi's sons Wensi and Ziran were both dismissed.

sentences.zh: 右相河間郡公李義府典選，恃中宮之勢，專以賣官為事，銓綜無次，怨讟盈路，上頗聞之，從容謂義府曰：「卿子及婿頗不謹，多為非法。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Li Yifu of Hejian Commandery, Duke, controlled selection; relying on the empress's power, he devoted himself to selling offices; appointments were without order and complaints filled the roads. The emperor had heard something of this and said calmly to Yifu, "Your sons and sons-in-law are rather unrestrained and do much that is unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu, Duke of Hejian and Right Chancellor, ran the civil service roster; leaning on the empress's influence, he sold offices wholesale, appointments were chaotic, and outrage filled the streets. The emperor had heard of it and said gently, "Your sons and sons-in-law are rather reckless and break the law often.

sentences.zh: 我尚為卿掩覆，卿宜戒之！」

translations.literal: I still cover this up for you—you should warn them!"
translations.idiomatic: I am still covering for you—you should rein them in!"

sentences.zh: 義府勃然變色，頸、頰俱張，曰：「誰告陛下？」

translations.literal: Yifu flushed and changed color, neck and cheeks swelling, and said, "Who told Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Yifu flushed dark red, his neck and cheeks swelling, and demanded, "Who told Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但我言如是，何必就我索其所從得邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I speak as I do—why must you press me for where I learned it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I speak as I choose—why must you demand my sources!"

sentences.zh: 義府殊不引咎，緩步而去。

translations.literal: Yifu showed no sign of accepting blame and walked away at an easy pace.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu offered no apology and strolled away.

sentences.zh: 上由是不悅。

translations.literal: From this the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's displeasure only grew.

sentences.zh: 望氣者杜元紀謂義府所居第有獄氣，宜積錢二十萬緡以厭之，義府信之，聚斂尤急。

translations.literal: The qi-diviner Du Yuanji told Yifu that his residence had the aura of prison and that he should amass two hundred thousand strings of cash to ward it off; Yifu believed him and squeezed revenue all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The geomancer Du Yuanji told Yifu his mansion bore the aura of imprisonment and that he should hoard two hundred thousand strings of cash to dispel it; Yifu believed him and extorted money more ruthlessly than ever.

sentences.zh: 義府居母喪，朔望給哭假，輒微服與元紀出城東，登古塚，候望氣色，或告義府窺覘災眚，陰有異圖。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, on the new and full moons when mourning leave was granted, Yifu would put on plain dress and go east of the city with Yuanji, climb an ancient mound, and watch the qi; someone reported that Yifu was spying on omens of disaster and harbored secret designs.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, on the days when leave for weeping was granted, Yifu would dress in plain clothes and go east of the city with Yuanji to climb an old tomb and read the heavens; someone accused him of watching for portents of calamity and plotting treason in secret.

sentences.zh: 又遣其子右司議郎津召長孫無忌之孫延，受其錢七百緡，除延司津監，右金吾倉曹參軍楊行穎告之。

translations.literal: He also sent his son Jin, Right Secretariat Discussant, to summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, accepted seven hundred strings of cash from him, and appointed Yan Superintendent of the River Pass; Right Jinwu Granary Officer Yang Xingying reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He also had his son Jin, a Right Secretariat discussant, summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, take seven hundred strings of cash from him, and appoint him River Pass superintendent; Yang Xingying, an officer of the Right Jinwu Guard, reported it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙丑，下義府獄，遣司刑太常伯劉祥道與御史、詳刑共鞫之，仍命司空李勣監焉。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yichou, Yifu was cast into prison; Minister of Punishments Liu Xiangdao was sent with censors and detailed examiners jointly to interrogate him, and Minister of Works Li Ji was ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yichou, Yifu was imprisoned; Liu Xiangdao of the Ministry of Punishments was sent with censors and judicial reviewers to try the case, with Minister of Works Li Ji ordered to oversee.

sentences.zh: 事皆有實。

translations.literal: The charges were all substantiated.
translations.idiomatic: Every charge proved true.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔義府除名，流巂州；

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict struck Yifu from the rolls and exiled him to Xizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, an edict struck Yifu from the registers and banished him to Xizhou;

sentences.zh: 津除名，流振州；

translations.literal: Jin was struck from the rolls and exiled to Zhen Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Jin was struck from the rolls and sent to Zhen Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 諸子及婿並除名，流庭州。

translations.literal: all his sons and sons-in-law were struck from the rolls and exiled to Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: all his sons and sons-in-law were struck from the rolls and exiled to Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝野莫不稱慶。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 或作河間道行軍元帥劉祥道破銅山大賊李義府露布，膀之通衢。

translations.literal: Someone composed a victory bulletin in the style of "Campaign Marshal Liu Xiangdao of Hejian Route crushes the great bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it in the public thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote a mock victory bulletin—"Campaign Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian route crushes the great bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain"—and posted it in the streets.

sentences.zh: 義府多取人奴婢，及敗，各散歸其家，故其露布云：「混奴婢而亂放，各識家而競入。」

translations.literal: Yifu had taken many people's slaves and bondmaids; when he fell, each scattered back to their homes, so the bulletin read, "Slaves and maids mixed together and released in confusion—each knew its home and rushed to enter."
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had seized many people's slaves; when he fell they scattered home, so the bulletin joked, "Slaves and maids released in a confused herd—each knew its master's door and rushed inside."

sentences.zh: 乙未，置雞林大都督府於新羅國，以金法敏為之。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Jilin Grand Protectorate was established in Silla, with Kim Beopmin as its head.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Jilin Grand Protectorate was set up in Silla, with Kim Beopmin appointed to head it.

sentences.zh: 丙午，蓬萊宮含元殿成，上始移仗居之，更命故宮曰西內。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Hanyuan Hall of Penglai Palace was completed; the emperor first moved the imperial presence to dwell there and renamed the former palace the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Hanyuan Hall of Penglai Palace was finished; the emperor moved the court there and renamed the old palace the Western Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊申，始御紫宸殿聽政。

translations.literal: On wushen, he first held court and heard affairs in the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, he held his first audience in the Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，柳州蠻酋吳君解反；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renwu, the Liuzhou barbarian chieftain Wu Junjie rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu, Wu Junjie, a tribal chief in Liuzhou, rose in revolt;

sentences.zh: 遣冀州長史劉伯英、右武衛將軍馮士翽發嶺南兵討之。

translations.literal: Liu Boying, chief administrator of Ji Prefecture, and You Wuwei General Feng Shixie were sent to raise Lingnan troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Boying, chief administrator of Ji Prefecture, and General Feng Shixie of the Right Wuwei Guard were dispatched to raise Lingnan troops against him.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃與吐谷渾互相攻，各遣使上表論曲直，更來求援；

translations.literal: Tibet and Tuyuhun attacked each other; each sent envoys with memorials arguing right and wrong and again came seeking aid;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet and Tuyuhun fought each other; each sent envoys with memorials pleading its case and again asked for Tang support;

sentences.zh: 上皆不許。

translations.literal: the emperor refused both.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused both sides.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾之臣素和貴有罪，逃奔吐蕃，具言吐谷渾虛實，吐蕃發兵擊吐谷渾，大破之，吐谷渾可汗曷缽與弘化公主帥數千帳棄國走依涼州，請徙居內地。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun minister Suhegui, guilty of a crime, fled to Tibet and fully disclosed Tuyuhun's strengths and weaknesses; Tibet raised troops, attacked Tuyuhun, and routed them. Tuyuhun Khan Hubo and Princess Honghua led several thousand tents in abandoning their state, fled to rely on Liang Prefecture, and asked to be moved within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Suhegui, a Tuyuhun minister who had committed a crime, fled to Tibet and revealed Tuyuhun's full situation; Tibet marched against Tuyuhun and crushed them. Khan Hubo and Princess Honghua abandoned their realm with several thousand tents, fled to Liang Prefecture, and asked to be resettled within Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 上以涼州都督鄭仁泰為青海道行軍大總管，帥右武衛將軍獨狐卿雲、辛文陵等分屯涼、鄯二州，以備吐蕃。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Liang Prefecture Commander Zheng Rentai Grand Commander of the Qinghai Route Campaign, leading You Wuwei Generals Dugu Qingyun, Xin Wenling, and others to garrison separately at Liang and Shan Prefectures against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Zheng Rentai, commander of Liang Prefecture, Grand Commander of the Qinghai route, with Generals Dugu Qingyun and Xin Wenling of the Right Wuwei Guard to hold Liang and Shan in readiness against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，又以左武衛大將軍蘇定方為安集大使，節度諸軍，為吐谷渾之援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, Zuo Wuwei Grand General Su Dingfang was also made Pacification Commissioner, directing all armies in aid of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Su Dingfang, grand general of the Left Wuwei Guard, was also appointed Pacification Commissioner to command all forces in support of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃祿東贊屯青海，遣使者論仲琮入見，表陳吐谷渾之罪，且請和親。

translations.literal: Tibet's Gar Tongtsen camped at Qinghai and sent the envoy Lun Zhongcong to audience, memorializing Tuyuhun's crimes and also requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen of Tibet encamped at Qinghai and sent Lun Zhongcong to court with a memorial denouncing Tuyuhun and asking for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上不許，遣左衛郎將劉文祥使於吐蕃，降璽書責讓之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent and sent Zuo Wei Commandant Liu Wenxiang as envoy to Tibet with an imperial letter rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and sent Commandant Liu Wenxiang of the Left Guard to Tibet with an imperial letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，戊申，上以海東累歲用兵，百姓困於徵調，士卒戰溺死者甚眾，詔罷三十六州所造船，遣司元太常伯竇德玄等分詣十道，問人疾苦，黜陟官吏。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on wushen, because the eastern sea region had seen years of campaigning, the people were distressed by levies, and many soldiers had died in battle or by drowning, an edict halted shipbuilding in thirty-six prefectures and sent Minister of Revenue Dou Dexuan and others separately to the ten circuits to inquire into people's hardships and promote or demote officials.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on wushen, with years of war in the eastern sea region, the people worn down by levies, and vast numbers of soldiers lost in battle and at sea, an edict halted shipbuilding in thirty-six prefectures and sent Dou Dexuan and others to the ten circuits to hear grievances and judge officials.

sentences.zh: 德玄，毅之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Dexuan was a great-grandson of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan was a great-grandson of Dou Yi.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，熊津道行軍總管、右威衛將軍孫仁師等破百濟餘眾及倭兵於白江，拔其周留城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuwu, Xiongjin Route Campaign Commander, You Weiwei General Sun Renshi, and others defeated Baekje remnants and Wa troops at the Baek River and took their city of Zhouliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuwu, Sun Renshi, campaign commander of the Xiongjin route and general of the Right Weiwei Guard, defeated Baekje remnants and Japanese forces at the Baek River and captured Zhouliu.

sentences.zh: 初，劉仁願、劉仁軌既克真峴城，詔孫仁師將兵浮海助之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Liu Renyuan and Liu Rengui had taken the city of Zhenxian, Sun Renshi was ordered to lead troops by sea to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Renyuan and Liu Rengui captured Zhenxian, Sun Renshi was ordered to bring troops by sea to their aid.

sentences.zh: 百濟王豐南引倭人以拒唐兵。

translations.literal: The king of Baekje, Buyeo Pung, brought in Wa men to resist the Tang army.
translations.idiomatic: King Buyeo Pung of Baekje brought in Japanese troops to resist the Tang.

sentences.zh: 仁師與仁願、仁軌合兵，勢大振。

translations.literal: Renshi joined forces with Renyuan and Rengui, and their power greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Renshi joined Renyuan and Rengui, and their combined strength surged.

sentences.zh: 諸將以加林城水陸之沖，欲先攻之，仁軌曰：「加林險固，急攻則傷士卒，緩之則曠日持久。

translations.literal: The generals, because Jialin City was a choke point by land and water, wished to attack it first; Rengui said, "Jialin is perilous and strong—if we press the attack we will harm the troops; if we go slowly the days will drag on.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to strike Jialin first, a hub of land and sea routes; Rengui said, "Jialin is strong—pressing the attack will cost men, while a slow siege will drag on forever.

sentences.zh: 周留城，虜之巢穴，群凶所聚，除惡務本，宜先攻之，若克周留，諸城自下。」

translations.literal: Zhouliu City is the enemy's lair where the wicked gather; in rooting out evil one must strike at the root—we should attack it first; if Zhouliu falls, the other cities will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Zhouliu is the enemy's nest where the ringleaders gather; to root out evil you must strike the core. Take Zhouliu first, and the rest will fall of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 於是仁師、仁願與新羅王法敏將陸軍以進，仁軌與別將杜爽、撫餘隆將水軍及糧船自熊津入白江，以會陸軍，同趣周留城。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renshi and Renyuan, with Silla King Beopmin, led the land army forward; Rengui with detached commanders Du Shuang and Buyu Yong led the navy and grain ships from Xiongjin into the Baek River to join the land force, all pressing on Zhouliu together.
translations.idiomatic: Renshi and Renyuan advanced overland with Silla's King Beopmin; Rengui, with Du Shuang and Buyu Yong, led the fleet and supply ships from Xiongjin into the Baek River to join the land force, and all converged on Zhouliu.

sentences.zh: 遇倭兵於白江口，四戰皆捷，焚其舟四百艘，煙炎灼天，海水皆赤。

translations.literal: They met Wa troops at the mouth of the Baek River; in four engagements all were victorious, four hundred of their ships were burned, smoke and flame scorched the sky, and the sea water turned red.
translations.idiomatic: At the mouth of the Baek River they met the Japanese fleet; four battles brought four victories, four hundred ships were burned, smoke blotted out the sky, and the sea ran red.

sentences.zh: 百濟王豐脫身奔高麗，王子忠勝、忠志等帥眾降，百濟盡平，唯別帥遲受信據任存城，不下。

translations.literal: The king of Baekje, Pung, escaped alone and fled to Goguryeo; princes Chungsung, Chungji, and others led the masses in surrender; Baekje was wholly pacified—only the detached commander Chi Suksin held out at Rencun City and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: King Pung fled alone to Goguryeo; princes Chungsung, Chungji, and others surrendered with their followers; Baekje was fully pacified—only the detached commander Chi Suksin still held Rencun and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 初，百濟西部人黑齒常之，長七尺餘，驍勇有謀略，仕百濟為達率兼郡將，猶中國刺史也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Heukchi Sangji of western Baekje, more than seven chi tall, brave and resourceful, had served Baekje as a dalsol combined with commandery general—the equivalent of a Chinese prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was Heukchi Sangji of western Baekje, over seven chi tall, fierce and shrewd, who had served Baekje as a dalsol and commandery general—the rough equivalent of a Tang prefect.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方克百濟，常之帥所部隨眾降。

translations.literal: When Su Dingfang conquered Baekje, Sangji led his command in surrendering with the masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Dingfang conquered Baekje, Sangji surrendered with his men along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 定方縶其王及太子，縱兵劫掠，壯者多死。

translations.literal: Dingfang bound their king and crown prince and let the troops plunder at will; many of the strong perished.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang bound the king and crown prince and let his troops loot freely; many able-bodied men died.

sentences.zh: 常之懼，與左右十餘人遁歸本部，收集亡散，保任存山，結柵以自固，旬月間歸附者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Sangji was afraid; with a dozen or so close followers he fled back to his home territory, gathered the scattered and lost, held Mount Rencun, built palisades to secure himself, and within a month and more more than thirty thousand came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Sangji fled in fear with a dozen companions to his home region, rallied the scattered, fortified Mount Rencun with palisades, and within a month had gathered more than thirty thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 定方遣兵攻之，常之拒戰，唐兵不利；

translations.literal: Dingfang sent troops to attack him; Sangji resisted, and the Tang army fared ill;
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang sent troops against him; Sangji fought back and the Tang forces came off badly;

sentences.zh: 常之復取二百餘城，定方不能克而還。

translations.literal: Sangji again took more than two hundred cities; Dingfang could not overcome him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sangji recovered more than two hundred towns; Dingfang could not break him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 常之與別部將沙吒相如各據險以應福信，百濟既敗，皆帥其眾降。

translations.literal: Sangji and the detached commander Shazha Xiangru each held perilous ground in response to Fukushin; after Baekje's defeat, both led their followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sangji and the detached commander Shazha Xiangru had each held strong positions in support of Fukushin; after Baekje's fall, both surrendered with their men.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌使常之、相如自將其眾，取任存城，仍以糧仗助之。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui had Sangji and Xiangru personally lead their followers to take Rencun City and also supplied them with grain and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui sent Sangji and Xiangru to lead their own men against Rencun and supplied them with grain and weapons.

sentences.zh: 孫仁帥曰：「此屬獸心，何可信也！」

translations.literal: Sun Renshi said, "These men have the hearts of beasts—how can they be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi said, "These men have the hearts of beasts—how can we trust them!"

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「吾觀二人皆忠勇有謀，敦信重義；

translations.literal: Rengui said, "I observe that both men are loyal, brave, and resourceful, sincere in faith and weighty in righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Rengui replied, "I see in both men loyalty, courage, and shrewdness, with a deep sense of honor;

sentences.zh: 但向者所托，未得其人，今正是其感激立效之時，不用疑也。」

translations.literal: only before those to whom they were entrusted were not the right men—now is exactly the time for them to repay gratitude and prove themselves at once; there is no need for doubt."
translations.idiomatic: only before they were given to the wrong commanders. Now is the moment for them to prove themselves in gratitude—there is no reason to doubt them."

sentences.zh: 遂給其糧仗，分兵隨之，攻拔任存城，遲受信棄妻子，奔高麗。

translations.literal: He then gave them grain and arms, detached troops to follow them, stormed and took Rencun City, and Chi Suksin abandoned wife and children and fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied them with grain and arms, detached troops to accompany them, and they stormed Rencun; Chi Suksin abandoned his family and fled to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 詔劉仁軌將兵鎮百濟，召孫仁帥、劉仁願還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Rengui to lead troops and garrison Baekje, and summoned Sun Renshi and Liu Renyuan back.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Liu Rengui in command of the Baekje garrison and recalled Sun Renshi and Liu Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 百濟兵火之餘，比屋凋殘，殭屍滿野。

translations.literal: After the fires of war in Baekje, house after house lay wasted and corpses filled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: After the fires of war, house after house lay in ruins and unburied dead filled the fields.

sentences.zh: 仁軌始命瘞骸骨，籍戶口，理村聚，署官長，通道塗，立橋樑，補堤堰，復陂塘，課耕桑，賑貧乏，養孤老，立唐社稷，頒正朔及廟諱；

translations.literal: Rengui first ordered the bones buried, households registered, villages and hamlets put in order, officials appointed, roads cleared, bridges built, dikes and weirs repaired, ponds and reservoirs restored, farming and sericulture urged, the poor relieved, orphans and aged supported, Tang altars of soil and grain established, and the correct calendar and taboo names of the imperial temple promulgated;
translations.idiomatic: Rengui ordered the dead buried, households registered, villages reorganized, local officials appointed, roads cleared, bridges built, dikes and ponds restored, farming encouraged, the poor relieved, orphans and the aged cared for, Tang altars established, and the imperial calendar and taboo names proclaimed;

sentences.zh: 百濟大悅，闔境各安其業。

translations.literal: Baekje greatly rejoiced, and throughout the territory each settled to his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje rejoiced, and throughout the land people returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 然後修屯田，儲糗糧，訓士卒，以圖高麗。

translations.literal: Then he developed military colonies, stored grain, trained soldiers, and planned against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Then he opened military colonies, stockpiled grain, trained troops, and turned his sights on Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 劉仁願至京帥，上問之曰：「卿在海東，前後奏事，皆合機宜，復有文理。

translations.literal: When Liu Renyuan reached the capital, the emperor asked him, "When you were in the eastern sea region, your memorials before and after all fit the moment and moreover had literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Renyuan reached the capital, the emperor asked him, "In the eastern campaigns your memorials were always timely and well written.

sentences.zh: 卿本武人，何能如是？」

translations.literal: You are originally a military man—how could you do thus?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a soldier by trade—how did you manage that?"

sentences.zh: 仁願曰：「此皆劉仁軌所為，非臣所及也。」

translations.literal: Renyuan said, "All this was Liu Rengui's doing—not within your servant's reach."
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan said, "That was all Liu Rengui's work—not mine."

sentences.zh: 上悅，加仁軌六階，正除帶方州刺史，為築第長安，厚賜其妻子，遣使繼璽書勞勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, raised Rengui six ranks, formally appointed him prefect of Daifang, built him a mansion in Chang'an, richly rewarded his wife and children, and sent envoys with successive imperial letters of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted Rengui six ranks, formally appointed him prefect of Daifang, built him a mansion in Chang'an, richly rewarded his family, and sent envoys with repeated letters of commendation.

sentences.zh: 上官儀曰：「仁軌遭黜削而能盡忠，仁願秉節制而能推賢，皆可謂君子矣。」

translations.literal: Shangguan Yi said, "Rengui, though demoted, could still give full loyalty; Renyuan, holding military authority, could yet recommend the worthy—both may be called gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi said, "Rengui remained loyal after demotion; Renyuan, holding command, praised his better—both are true gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳朔，詔太子每五日於光順門內視諸司奏事，其事之小者，皆委太子決之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day xinsi, an edict ordered that every five days the crown prince should within the Guangshun Gate review the memorials of the various offices; lesser matters were all entrusted to the crown prince to decide.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of xinsi, an edict required the crown prince every five days to review ministry memorials within the Guangshun Gate; minor matters were left entirely to his decision.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，詔改來年元。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, an edict changed the reign title for the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, an edict proclaimed a new reign title for the following year.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以安西都護高賢為行軍總管，將兵擊弓月以救于闐。

translations.literal: On renyin, Anxi Protector Gao Xian was made campaign commander and led troops to attack the Gongyue tribe to relieve Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Gao Xian, protector of Anxi, was appointed campaign commander to strike the Gongyue and relieve Khotan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大食擊波斯、拂菻，破之；

translations.literal: That year the Arabs attacked Persia and Byzantium and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: That year the Arabs attacked Persia and Byzantium and overran them;

sentences.zh: 南侵婆羅門，吞滅諸胡，勝兵四十餘萬。

translations.literal: they invaded south into Brahman lands, swallowed the various Hu states, and had more than four hundred thousand victorious troops.
translations.idiomatic: marched south into India, swallowed the western realms, and fielded more than four hundred thousand battle-ready troops.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，改雲中都護府為單于大都護府，以殷王旭輪為單于大都護。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiazi, the Yunzhong Protectorate was changed to the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, with Prince Yin Xulun as Grand Protector of the Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiazi, the Yunzhong Protectorate became the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, with Prince Yin Xulun named Grand Protector of the Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 初，李靖破突厥，遷三百帳於雲中城，阿史德氏為其長。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Jing defeated the Turks, three hundred tents were moved to Yunzhong City, with the Ashide clan as their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Li Jing's defeat of the Turks, three hundred tents were resettled at Yunzhong, headed by the Ashide clan.

sentences.zh: 至是，部落漸眾，阿史德氏詣闕，請如胡法立親王為可汗以統之。

translations.literal: By this time the tribe had gradually grown numerous; the Ashide clan came to court and asked that, according to barbarian custom, an imperial prince be established as khan to rule them.
translations.idiomatic: By then the tribe had grown large; the Ashide came to court and asked that an imperial prince be made khan in the barbarian fashion to rule them.

sentences.zh: 上召見，謂曰：「今之可汗，古之單于也。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned them to audience and said, "Today's khan is the chanyu of old."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them and said, "The khan of today is the chanyu of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 故更為單于都護府，而使殷王遙領之。

translations.literal: Therefore it was again made the Chanyu Protectorate, with the Prince of Yin holding it at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the office was renamed the Chanyu Protectorate, with the Prince of Yin holding the title in absentia.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊子，上行幸萬年宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuzi, the emperor traveled to the Wannian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuzi, the emperor visited the Wannian Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬子，衛州刺史道孝王元慶薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi, Prince Dao Xiao Yuanqing, prefect of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi, Prince Dao Xiao Yuanqing, prefect of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 丙午，魏州刺史郇公孝協坐贓，賜死。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Duke of Xun Xiaoxie, prefect of Wei, was convicted of corruption and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Duke of Xun Xiaoxie, prefect of Wei, was convicted of graft and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 司宗卿隴西王傅義等奏孝協父叔良死王事，孝協無兄弟，恐絕嗣。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Prince of Longxi Fu Yi and others memorialized that Xiaoxie's father Shuliang had died in the king's service, that Xiaoxie had no brothers, and that the line might be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi, Prince of Longxi and director of the imperial clan, and others argued that Xiaoxie's father Shuliang had died in imperial service, that Xiaoxie had no brothers, and that the line might die out.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「畫一之法，不以親疏異制，苟害百姓，雖皇太子亦所不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Uniform law does not vary the standard for near or far kin; if one harms the people, even the crown prince is not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The law is one for all, kinship notwithstanding; whoever harms the people—even the crown prince—will not be spared.

sentences.zh: 孝協有一子，何憂乏祀乎！」

translations.literal: Xiaoxie has one son—why worry that sacrifices will fail!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie has a son—why fear the ancestral rites will lapse!"

sentences.zh: 孝協竟自盡於第。

translations.literal: Xiaoxie in the end killed himself at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie ultimately took his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊申朔，遂州刺史許悼王孝薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day wushen, Prince Xu Dao Xiao, prefect of Suizhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of wushen, Prince Xu Dao Xiao, prefect of Suizhou, died.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，於昆明之弄棟川置姚州都督府。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Yao Prefecture Commandery was established at Nongdong River in Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Yao Prefecture commandery was established on the Nongdong River in Kunming.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁未朔，詔以三年正月有事於岱宗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day dingwei, an edict ordered rites at Mount Dai in the first month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of dingwei, an edict set rites at Mount Tai for the first month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙子，車駕還京師，幸舊宅，留七月；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingzi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital, visited the old residence, and stayed seven months;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingzi, the emperor returned to the capital, visited his old home, and stayed seven months;

sentences.zh: 壬午，還蓬萊宮。

translations.literal: on renwu he returned to Penglai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: on renwu he returned to Penglai Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以司列太常伯劉祥道兼右相，大司憲竇德玄為司元太常伯、檢校左相。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Liu Xiangdao, Minister of Rites for the Array, was also made Right Chancellor; Grand Censor Dou Dexuan was made Minister of Revenue and Acting Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Liu Xiangdao, minister of rites for the array, was also appointed Right Chancellor; Grand Censor Dou Dexuan became Minister of Revenue and acting Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚辰，檢校熊津都督劉仁軌上言：「臣伏睹所存戍兵，疲羸者多，勇健者少，衣服貧敝，唯思西歸，無心展效。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengchen, Acting Xiongjin Commander Liu Rengui memorialized: "Your servant has observed that among the garrison troops now on hand, many are worn and weak, few are brave and strong; their clothing is poor and threadbare; they think only of returning west and have no heart to show merit.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengchen, Acting Commander Liu Rengui of Xiongjin reported: "I find many of the garrison troops worn and weak, few fit for battle; their clothes are ragged; they think only of going home and have no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 臣問以『往在海西，見百姓人人應募，爭欲從軍，或請自辦衣糧，謂之「義征」，何為今日士卒如此？』

translations.literal: I asked, 'In the past at Haixi I saw common people all volunteering, competing to join the army, some asking to supply their own clothing and grain—called "righteous levies"—why are today's soldiers thus?'
translations.idiomatic: I asked, 'In the past on the western coast everyone rushed to enlist, some even offering to supply their own gear—volunteer campaigns—why are today's soldiers so unlike that?'

sentences.zh: 鹹言：『今日官府與曩時不同，人心亦殊。

translations.literal: They all said, 'Today's government offices are not as in former times, and hearts are different too.'
translations.idiomatic: They all said, 'The government today is not what it was, and men's hearts have changed.'

sentences.zh: 曩時東西征役，身沒王事，並蒙敕使弔祭，追贈官爵，或以死者官爵回授之弟，凡渡遼海者，皆賜勳一轉。

translations.literal: In former times, for eastern and western campaigns, those who died in the king's service all received imperial envoys for mourning sacrifices, posthumous ranks and titles, or the dead man's rank and title were transferred to a younger brother; all who crossed the Liao Sea were granted one step in merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the old days, men who died on campaign received imperial mourners, posthumous honors, or their rank passed to a brother; everyone who crossed the Liao Sea earned a merit step.

sentences.zh: 自顯慶五年以來，徵人屢經渡海，官不記錄，其死者亦無人誰何。

translations.literal: Since the fifth year of Xianqing, levied men have repeatedly crossed the sea, but the offices keep no record, and for the dead no one is held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fifth year of Xianqing, conscripts have crossed the sea again and again without official record, and no one answers for the dead.

sentences.zh: 州縣每發百姓為兵，其壯而富者，行錢參逐，皆亡匿得免；

translations.literal: Whenever prefectures and counties draft common people as soldiers, the strong and wealthy, by paying money to follow the levy officers, all hide and escape;
translations.idiomatic: When counties draft soldiers, the strong and wealthy bribe the levy officers and hide to escape;

sentences.zh: 貧者身雖老弱，被發即行。

translations.literal: the poor, though old or weak in body, once the summons is issued must go.
translations.idiomatic: the poor, however old or frail, are marched off the moment the summons comes.

sentences.zh: 頃者破百濟及平壤苦戰，當是時，將帥號令，許以勳賞，無所不至；

translations.literal: Recently in the hard fighting that broke Baekje and Pyongyang, at that time the generals' orders promised merit rewards—nothing was withheld;
translations.idiomatic: In the recent hard fighting against Baekje and Pyongyang, commanders promised every sort of merit reward;

sentences.zh: 及達西岸，惟聞枷鎖推禁，奪賜破勳，州縣追呼，無以自存，公私因弊，不可悉言。

translations.literal: but on reaching the western shore one heard only of shackles and imprisonment, seized rewards and broken merit registers, prefectures and counties in pursuit—no way to live; public and private alike were ruined beyond full telling.
translations.idiomatic: but once they reached the western shore they met only shackles, stripped rewards, voided merit rolls, and county collectors hounding them—public and private ruin beyond words.

sentences.zh: 以是昨發海西之日，已有逃亡自殘者，非獨至海外而然也。

translations.literal: Thus from the day they set out from Haixi yesterday there were already those who fled or maimed themselves—not only after reaching overseas.
translations.idiomatic: So even when they left the western coast, men were already fleeing or maiming themselves—not only overseas.

sentences.zh: 又，本因征役勳級以為榮寵；

translations.literal: Moreover, men once took campaign merit ranks as honor and favor;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, campaign merit was once a mark of honor;

sentences.zh: 而比年出征，皆使勳官挽引，勞苦與白丁無殊，百姓不願從軍，率皆由此。』

translations.literal: but in recent years on campaign, men of merit rank are all made to haul carts—their toil no different from common conscripts; the people do not wish to serve in the army, and this is generally the reason.'
translations.idiomatic: but lately even men of merit are made to haul supply carts like common conscripts—that is chiefly why the people refuse to serve.'

sentences.zh: 臣又問：『曩日士卒留鎮五年，尚得支濟，今爾等始經一年，何為如此單露？』

translations.literal: I also asked, 'In former days soldiers garrisoned five years and could still get by; you have been here only one year—why are you so destitute?'
translations.idiomatic: I also asked, 'Soldiers used to garrison five years and still manage; you have been here only one year—why are you so destitute?'

sentences.zh: 鹹言：『初發家日，惟令備一年資裝；

translations.literal: They all said, 'On the day we left home we were told to prepare only one year's supplies;
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'When we left home we were told to bring only one year's supplies;

sentences.zh: 今已二年，未有還期。』

translations.literal: it is already two years and there is no date of return.'
translations.idiomatic: it has been two years with no word of return.'

sentences.zh: 臣檢校軍士所留衣，今冬僅可充事，來秋以往，全無準擬。

translations.literal: Your servant has inspected the clothing the soldiers have left; this winter it will barely suffice, but from next autumn onward there is no provision at all.
translations.idiomatic: I have inspected the soldiers' remaining clothing: it will barely last this winter; after next autumn there is nothing.

sentences.zh: 陛下留兵海外，欲殄滅高麗。

translations.literal: Your Majesty keeps troops overseas wishing to exterminate Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps troops overseas to destroy Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 百濟、高麗，舊相黨援，倭人雖遠，亦共為影響，若無鎮兵，還成一國。

translations.literal: Baekje and Goguryeo have long aided each other; though the Wa people are far off, they too act in concert—without garrison troops they would again become one state.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje and Goguryeo have long been allies; though Japan is distant, it acts with them—without a garrison they would reunite as one power.

sentences.zh: 今既資戍守，又置屯田，所借士卒同心同德，而眾有此議，何望成功！

translations.literal: Now you rely on garrison defense and have also established military colonies—the troops you borrow should be of one heart and one virtue—yet the masses speak thus; how can success be hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: You rely on garrisons and military colonies and need soldiers of one mind—yet they speak like this; how can you hope to succeed!

sentences.zh: 自非有所更張，厚加慰勞，明賞重罰以起士心，若止如今日已前處置，恐師眾疲老，立效無日。

translations.literal: Unless there is reform, generous consolation and rewards, clear rewards and heavy punishments to rouse the soldiers' hearts—if matters stop as handled until today—I fear the army will grow weary and aged, and the day of merit will never come.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you reform policy, comfort the troops generously, and enforce clear rewards and stern punishments, the army will grow old and useless before it ever wins anything.

sentences.zh: 逆耳之事，或無人為陛下盡言，故臣披露肝膽，昧死奏陳。」

translations.literal: Unpleasant matters perhaps have no one to speak them fully to Your Majesty; therefore your servant lays bare heart and gall and, risking death, presents this memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Harsh truths may go unspoken at court; therefore I lay bare my heart and risk my life to report them."

sentences.zh: 上深納其言，遣右威衛將軍劉仁願將兵渡海以代舊鎮之兵，仍敕仁軌俱還。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words, sent You Weiwei General Liu Renyuan to lead troops across the sea to replace the old garrison, and also ordered Rengui to return as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice to heart, sent Liu Renyuan of the Right Weiwei Guard across the sea to relieve the old garrison, and ordered Rengui home as well.

sentences.zh: 仁軌謂仁願曰：「國家懸軍海外，欲以經略高麗，其事非易。

translations.literal: Rengui said to Renyuan, "The state has its army hanging overseas, wishing to plan against Goguryeo—the matter is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui told Renyuan, "The state has hung its army overseas to master Goguryeo—that is no easy task.

sentences.zh: 今收穫未畢，而軍吏與士卒一時代去，軍將又歸；

translations.literal: The harvest is not yet finished, yet officers and soldiers are all to be replaced at once, and the army commander is also to return;
translations.idiomatic: The harvest is not in, yet officers and men are to be replaced all at once and the commander recalled;

sentences.zh: 夷人新服，眾心未安，必將生變。

translations.literal: the barbarians have newly submitted and hearts are not yet settled—trouble will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: the barbarians have only just submitted and are not yet settled—trouble is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 不如且留舊兵，漸令收穫，辦具資糧，節級遣還；

translations.literal: it would be better to keep the old troops for now, gradually have them finish the harvest, prepare supplies, and send men back in stages;
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep the old troops, finish the harvest, gather supplies, and rotate men home in stages;

sentences.zh: 軍將且留鎮撫，未可還也。」

translations.literal: the army commander should remain to pacify—he must not return yet."
translations.idiomatic: the commander should stay to keep order—you must not leave yet."

sentences.zh: 仁願曰：「吾前還海西，大遭讒謗，雲吾多留兵眾，謀據海東，幾不免禍。

translations.literal: Renyuan said, "When I returned from Haixi before I suffered great slander—they said I kept too many troops and plotted to hold the eastern sea, and I nearly escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan said, "When I last came back from the west coast I was slandered for keeping too many troops and plotting to seize the eastern sea—I nearly came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今日唯知准敕，豈敢擅有所為！」

translations.literal: Today I know only to follow the edict—how would I dare act on my own!"
translations.idiomatic: Today I follow the edict alone—how dare I act on my own!"

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「人臣苟利於國，知無不為，豈恤其私！」

translations.literal: Rengui said, "If a subject profits the state, he does whatever he knows without regard for private interest!"
translations.idiomatic: Rengui said, "A minister who serves the state does what must be done without thought for himself!"

sentences.zh: 乃上表陳便宜，自請留鎮海東。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial setting forth what was expedient and asked to remain and garrison the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized on what was expedient and asked to remain in command of the eastern sea.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 仍以扶餘隆為熊津都尉，使招輯其餘眾。

translations.literal: Buyu Yong was also made Xiongjin Commandant to gather and settle the remaining masses.
translations.idiomatic: Buyu Yong was also made commandant of Xiongjin to rally the remaining people.

sentences.zh: 初，武后能屈身忍辱，奉順上意，故上排群議而立之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Wu could humble herself and endure insult, obeying the emperor's wishes, and so the emperor set aside the group's objections and established her;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Wu had humbled herself and endured slights, deferring to the emperor's wishes, and so he overrode opposition to make her empress;

sentences.zh: 及得志，專作威福，上欲有所為，動為后所制，上不勝其忿。

translations.literal: once she had her way she monopolized might and blessings; whenever the emperor wished to act he was at once constrained by the empress, and the emperor could not contain his anger.
translations.idiomatic: once secure she ruled arbitrarily; whatever the emperor wished to do the empress blocked, until his anger could no longer be contained.

sentences.zh: 有道士郭行真，出入禁中，嘗為厭勝之術，宦者王伏勝發之。

translations.literal: There was the Daoist Guo Xingzhen, who went in and out of the inner palace and had practiced sorcery for domination; eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed him.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Guo Xingzhen had been entering the inner palace and practicing sorcery; the eunuch Wang Fusheng exposed him.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，密召西召侍郎、同東西台三品上官儀議之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and secretly summoned Western Office Vice Director, Third Rank Associate Shangguan Yi to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and secretly summoned Shangguan Yi, Vice Director of the Western Office and Third Rank Associate, to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 儀因言：「皇后專恣，海內所不與，請廢之。」

translations.literal: Yi thereupon said, "The empress is willful and arbitrary—what the realm will not tolerate; I ask that she be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The empress is tyrannical—the realm will not bear her; depose her."

sentences.zh: 上意亦以為然，即命儀草詔。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind also agreed and he at once ordered Yi to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Yi to draft the deposition edict.

sentences.zh: 左右奔告於后，后遽詣上自訴。

translations.literal: Attendants ran to tell the empress; the empress hurried to the emperor to plead her own case.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants ran to warn the empress; she rushed to the emperor to plead her case.

sentences.zh: 詔草猶在上所，上羞縮不忍，復待之如初；

translations.literal: The draft edict was still with the emperor; ashamed and shrinking, he could not bear it and treated her again as before;
translations.idiomatic: The draft was still in his hands; ashamed and unable to go through with it, he treated her as before;

sentences.zh: 猶恐后怨怒，因紿之曰：「我初無此心，皆上官儀教我。」

translations.literal: still fearing the empress's anger, he deceived her, saying, "I never had this intent at first—it was all Shangguan Yi who taught me."
translations.idiomatic: still fearing her wrath, he lied: "I never meant it—Shangguan Yi put me up to it."

sentences.zh: 儀先為陳王咨議，與王伏勝俱事故太子忠，后於是使許敬宗誣奏儀、伏勝與忠謀大逆。

translations.literal: Yi had earlier been adviser to Prince of Chen and, with Wang Fusheng, had both served the former crown prince Zhong; the empress then had Xu Jingzong falsely memorialize that Yi, Fusheng, and Zhong plotted great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had been adviser to the Prince of Chen; he and Wang Fusheng had both served the former crown prince Zhong; the empress had Xu Jingzong accuse them of plotting treason with Zhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，儀下獄，與其子庭芝、王伏勝皆死，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Yi was cast into prison; he, his son Tingzhi, and Wang Fusheng all died, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Yi was imprisoned; he, his son Tingzhi, and Wang Fusheng were all executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 戊子，賜忠死於流所。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Zhong was granted death at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Zhong was ordered to take his own life in exile.

sentences.zh: 右相劉祥道坐與儀善，罷政事，為司禮太常伯，左肅機鄭欽泰等朝士流貶者甚眾，皆坐與儀交通故也。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Liu Xiangdao, convicted of friendship with Yi, was removed from government affairs and made Minister of Rites; Zuo Suji Zheng Qintai and many court gentlemen were exiled and demoted—all for having had dealings with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Liu Xiangdao, punished for friendship with Yi, left the government and became Minister of Rites; Zheng Qintai and many courtiers were exiled—all for ties to Yi.

sentences.zh: 自是上每視事，則后垂簾於後，政無大小皆與聞之。

translations.literal: From this whenever the emperor held court the empress hung a curtain behind and heard all affairs great and small.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the emperor held court the empress sat behind a curtain and heard every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 天下大權，悉歸中宮，黜陟、生殺，決於其口，天子拱手而已，中外謂之二聖。

translations.literal: Great power under heaven all returned to the inner palace; promotion and demotion, life and death, were decided at her mouth—the Son of Heaven merely folded his hands—and within and without they called them the Two Sages.
translations.idiomatic: All power passed to the inner palace; promotion, demotion, life, and death were hers to decree while the emperor stood idle; court and country spoke of the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 太子右中護、檢校西台侍郎樂彥瑋、西台侍郎孫處約並同東西台三品。

translations.literal: Crown Prince's Right Central Guard, Acting Western Office Vice Director Yue Yanwei, and Western Office Vice Director Sun Chuyue were all made Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yanwei, crown prince's right central guard and acting vice director of the Western Office, and Sun Chuyue, vice director of the Western Office, were all appointed Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯，吐蕃遣使入見，請復與吐谷渾和親，仍求赤水地畜牧，上不許。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, Tibet sent envoys to audience, asking to restore marriage ties with Tuyuhun and also seeking pasture land at Chishui; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, Tibet sent envoys asking to renew ties with Tuyuhun and for pasture at Chishui; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，車駕發京師，丁酉，至合璧宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renwu, the imperial carriage departed the capital; on dingyou it reached the Hebi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu, the emperor left the capital; on dingyou he reached Hebi Palace.

sentences.zh: 上語及隋煬帝，謂侍臣曰：「煬帝拒諫而亡，朕常以為戒，虛心求諫；

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of Emperor Yang of Sui and told his attending ministers, "Yang rejected remonstrance and perished—I constantly take this as a warning and seek remonstrance with an open heart;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Emperor Yang of Sui, the emperor told his ministers, "Yang perished because he rejected counsel; I take that as my warning and welcome frank advice;

sentences.zh: 而竟無諫者，何也？」

translations.literal: yet in the end there are no remonstrators—why?"
translations.idiomatic: yet no one remonstrates—why?"

sentences.zh: 李勣對曰：「陛下所為盡善，群臣無得而諫。」

translations.literal: Li Ji replied, "Your Majesty's actions are all good—the ministers have nothing by which to remonstrate."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji replied, "Your Majesty does nothing that admits of criticism—the ministers have nothing to remonstrate about."

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，以兼司戎太常伯姜恪同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, Acting Minister of War Jiang Ke was made Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, Jiang Ke, acting minister of war, was appointed Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 恪，寶誼之子也。

translations.literal: Ke was the son of Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was a son of Jiang Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 辛未，東都乾元殿成。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Qianyuan Hall of the Eastern Capital was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Qianyuan Hall in the Eastern Capital was completed.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬申朔，車駕至東都。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day renshen, the imperial carriage reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the new moon of renshen, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 疏勒弓月引吐蕃侵于闐。

translations.literal: Shule's Gongyue tribe led Tibet to invade Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyue of Shule led Tibet in an attack on Khotan.

sentences.zh: 敕西州都督崔知辯、左武衛將軍曹繼叔將兵救之。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Xizhou Commander Cui Zhibian and Zuo Wuwei General Cao Jishu to lead troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhibian, commander of Xizhou, and Cao Jishu, general of the Left Wuwei Guard, were ordered to relieve Khotan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，左侍極陸敦信檢校右相；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuchen, Zuo Shiji Lu Dunxin was made Acting Right Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuchen, Lu Dunxin of the Left Shiji was made acting Right Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 西台侍郎孫處約、太子右中護、檢校西台侍郎樂彥瑋並罷政事。

translations.literal: Western Office Vice Director Sun Chuyue and Crown Prince's Right Central Guard, Acting Western Office Vice Director Yue Yanwei were all removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuyue, vice director of the Western Office, and Yue Yanwei, crown prince's right central guard and acting vice director of the Western Office, were all dismissed from government.

sentences.zh: 秘閣郎中李淳風以傅仁均《戊寅歷》推步浸疏，乃增損劉焯《皇極歷》，更撰《麟德歷》；

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant Li Chunfeng, finding Fu Renjun's Wuyin Calendar growing loose in its calculations, augmented and reduced Liu Zhuo's Huangji Calendar and newly composed the Qinde Calendar;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng of the Secretariat, finding Fu Renjun's Wuyin Calendar increasingly inaccurate, revised Liu Zhuo's Huangji Calendar and composed the new Qinde Calendar;

sentences.zh: 五月，辛卯，行之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinmao, it was put into use.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinmao, it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，兗州都督鄧康王元裕薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, Prince of Deng Kang Yuan Yu, commander of Yan Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, Prince Deng Kang Yuan Yu, commander of Yan Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 上命熊津都尉扶餘隆與新羅王法敏釋去舊怨；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiongjin Commandant Buyu Yong and Silla King Beopmin to release old grievances;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Buyu Yong of Xiongjin and King Beopmin of Silla to bury old grievances;

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，同盟於熊津城。

translations.literal: in the eighth month, on renzi, they allied at Xiongjin City.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month, on renzi, they swore alliance at Xiongjin.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌以新羅、百濟、耽羅、倭國使者浮海西還，會祠泰山，高麗亦遣太子福男來侍祠。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui, with envoys from Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Wa returning by sea from the west, met the sacrifice at Mount Tai; Goguryeo also sent Crown Prince Funan to attend the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui brought envoys from Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Japan home by sea for the Mount Tai rites; Goguryeo also sent Crown Prince Funan to attend.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，皇后表稱「封禪舊儀，祭皇地示氏，太后昭配，而令公卿行事，禮有未發，至日，妾請帥內外命婦奠獻。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, the empress memorialized, "In the old feng and shan rites, when sacrificing to the Queen of Earth, the Grand Empress Dowager was the illustrious consort, yet public ministers performed the act—the ritual had not been fully expressed; on the day, your concubine asks to lead the inner and outer titled women in offering libations."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, the empress memorialized: "In the old feng and shan rites the sacrifice to Earth paired the Grand Empress Dowager, yet ministers performed the rite—the ceremony was incomplete; on the day, I ask to lead the court ladies in the offerings."

sentences.zh: 詔：「禪社首以皇后為亞獻，越國太妃燕氏為終獻。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "At the shan at Mount Sheshou the empress shall be the secondary offerer and Grand Princess of Yue, Lady Yan, the final offerer."
translations.idiomatic: An edict named the empress secondary offerer at the shan on Mount Sheshou and Grand Princess Yan of Yue final offerer."

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔：「封禪壇所設上帝、后土位，先用蒿秸、陶匏等，並宜改用茵褥、罍爵，其諸郊祀亦宜准此。」

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict said, "At the feng and shan altars the places set for the Supreme Lord and Queen of Earth formerly used wormwood stalks, pottery, gourds, and the like—all should be changed to mats and bronze goblets; other suburban sacrifices should follow this standard."
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, an edict ordered that at the feng and shan altars the places for Heaven and Earth, formerly furnished with wormwood and pottery, should use mats and bronze vessels instead, and other suburban rites should follow suit."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「自今郊廟享宴，文舞用《功成慶善之樂》，武舞用《神功破陳之樂》。」

translations.literal: Another edict said, "From now on at suburban and temple banquets, the civil dance shall use the music 'Achievement Complete, Goodness Celebrated,' and the military dance the music 'Divine Merit, Chen Broken.'"
translations.idiomatic: Another edict decreed that at suburban and temple banquets the civil dance should use Achievement Complete, Goodness Celebrated and the military dance Divine Merit, Chen Broken."

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上發東都，從駕文武儀仗，數百里不絕。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the emperor departed the Eastern Capital; civil and military in the entourage with ceremonial guards stretched for several hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the emperor left the Eastern Capital; the civil and military procession with ceremonial guards stretched for hundreds of li without end.

sentences.zh: 列營置幕，彌亙原野。

translations.literal: They arrayed camps and pitched tents, filling the wild plains.
translations.idiomatic: Camps and tents were set up, stretching across the open countryside.

sentences.zh: 東自高麗，西至波斯、烏長諸國朝會者，各帥其屬扈從，穹廬毳幕，牛羊駝馬，填咽道路。

translations.literal: From Goguryeo in the east to Persia, Wuchang, and other states coming to the court assembly, each led their followers in attendance; domed tents and felt pavilions, cattle, sheep, camels, and horses filled and choked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from as far east as Goguryeo and as far west as Persia and Wuchang, each with retinues in attendance; yurts and felt tents, cattle, sheep, camels, and horses choked the roads.

sentences.zh: 時比歲豐稔，米斗至五錢，麥、豆不列於市。

translations.literal: At the time harvests had been abundant year after year; a dou of rice sold for as little as five cash, and wheat and beans were not listed in the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests had been abundant for years; a dou of rice sold for as little as five cash, and wheat and beans scarcely appeared in the markets.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子，上至濮陽，竇德玄騎從。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, the emperor reached Puyang; Dou Dexuan rode in the entourage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, the emperor reached Puyang, with Dou Dexuan riding in attendance.

sentences.zh: 上問：「濮陽謂之帝丘，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "Puyang is called Diqiu—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Puyang is called Diqiu, the Mound of the Emperor—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 德玄不能對。

translations.literal: Dou Dexuan could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Dexuan could not answer.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗自後躍馬而前曰：「昔顓頊居此，故謂之帝丘。」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong from behind spurred his horse forward and said, "In antiquity Zhuanxu dwelt here, and so it is called Diqiu."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong spurred his horse forward from the rear and said, "Zhuanxu once dwelt here, and so it is called Diqiu, the Mound of the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 上稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 敬宗退，謂人曰：「大臣不可以無學；

translations.literal: Jingzong withdrew and said to others, "A great minister must not be without learning;
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong withdrew, he told others, "A great minister cannot be without learning;

sentences.zh: 吾見德玄不能對，心實羞之。」

translations.literal: when I saw Dexuan unable to answer, I was truly ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: when I saw Dexuan unable to answer, I was truly ashamed."

sentences.zh: 德玄聞之，曰：「人各有能有不能，吾不強對以所不知，此吾所能也。」

translations.literal: When Dexuan heard this, he said, "Each man has what he can and cannot do; I do not force an answer to what I do not know—this is what I can do."
translations.idiomatic: When Dexuan heard this, he said, "Each man has his strengths and his limits; I do not pretend to know what I do not know—that is my virtue."

sentences.zh: 李勣曰：「敬宗多聞，信美矣；

translations.literal: Li Ji said, "Jingzong is widely learned—indeed admirable;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji said, "Jingzong is widely learned—that is admirable indeed;

sentences.zh: 德玄之言亦善也。」

translations.literal: Dexuan's words are also good."
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan's reply is also sound."

sentences.zh: 壽張人張公藝九世同居，齊、隋、唐皆旌表其門。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongyi of Shouzhang, nine generations living together; Qi, Sui, and Tang all honored his gate with commemorative marks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongyi of Shouzhang had nine generations living under one roof; the Qi, Sui, and Tang dynasties all honored his household with commemorative plaques.

sentences.zh: 上過壽張，幸其宅，問所以能共居之故，公藝書「忍」字百餘以進。

translations.literal: The emperor passed through Shouzhang, visited his home, and asked the reason they could live together; Gongyi wrote the character "ren" more than a hundred times and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: “When the emperor passed through Shouzhang, he visited Gongyi's home and asked how so many generations could live together; Gongyi wrote the character for forbearance more than a hundred times and presented them.”

sentences.zh: 上善之，賜以縑帛。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and bestowed silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and bestowed silk upon him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，車駕至齊州，留十日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, the imperial carriage reached Qizhou and stayed ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, the emperor reached Qizhou and remained ten days.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，發靈巖頓，至泰山下，有司於山南為圓壇，山上為登封壇，社首山上為降禪方壇。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the procession departed from Lingyan station and reached the foot of Mount Tai; officials built a round altar south of the mountain, an ascent-and-sealing altar on the summit, and a square altar for the descent rite on Mount Sheshou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the emperor left Lingyan station and reached the foot of Mount Tai; officials erected a round altar south of the mountain, a sealing altar on the summit, and a square altar for the descent rite on Mount Sheshou.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊辰朔，上祀昊天上帝於泰山南。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, new moon of wuchen, the emperor sacrificed to August Heaven on the south of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of wuchen, the emperor sacrificed to August Heaven south of Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 己巳，登泰山，封玉牒，上帝冊藏以玉匱，配帝冊藏以金匱，皆纏以金繩，封以金泥，印以玉璽，藏以石□感。

translations.literal: On jisi, he ascended Mount Tai and sealed the jade document; the Jade Emperor's text was stored in a jade casket and the associated deity's text in a gold casket; all were wrapped with gold cord, sealed with gold paste, stamped with a jade seal, and stored in a stone chamber/casket (lacuna).
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, he ascended Mount Tai and sealed the jade memorial; the text to August Heaven was placed in a jade casket and the text to the associated deity in a gold casket; all were bound with gold cord, sealed with gold paste, stamped with a jade seal, and deposited in a stone chamber/casket (lacuna).

sentences.zh: 庚午，降禪於社首，祭皇地祇。

translations.literal: On gengwu, he performed the descent rite at Sheshou and sacrificed to August Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, he performed the descent rite at Mount Sheshou and sacrificed to August Earth.

sentences.zh: 上初獻畢，執事者皆趨下。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished the first offering, all officiants hurried down.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had completed the first offering, all officiants hurried down from the altar.

sentences.zh: 宦者執帷，皇后升壇亞獻，帷帟皆以錦繡為之；

translations.literal: Eunuchs held curtains; the empress ascended the altar for the secondary offering; curtains and canopies were all made of brocade and embroidery;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs held the curtains as the empress ascended the altar for the secondary offering; all curtains and canopies were of brocade and embroidery;

sentences.zh: 酌酒，實俎豆，登歌，皆用宮人。

translations.literal: Pouring wine, filling vessels, and singing the ascent hymn—all were done by palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring wine, filling the ritual vessels, and singing the ascent hymn were all performed by palace women.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上御朝覲壇，受朝賀；

translations.literal: On renshen, the emperor took the altar of imperial audience and received congratulatory obeisances;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the emperor took his seat on the audience altar and received the court's congratulations;

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: He amnestied the realm and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 文武官三品已上賜爵一等，四品已下加一階。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of third rank and above were granted one grade of nobility; fourth rank and below received one step in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of third rank and above were granted one grade of nobility; those of fourth rank and below received one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 先是階無泛加，皆以勞考敘進，至五品三品，仍奏取進止，至是始有泛階，比及末年，服緋者滿朝矣。

translations.literal: Previously there had been no blanket promotions in rank—all advancement was by merit evaluation; for fifth through third rank, memorials still required approval. From this time blanket promotions began, and by the end of the reign those wearing scarlet filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Previously ranks were never raised across the board—all advancement went by merit review, and even for fifth through third rank a memorial still required imperial approval. From this time blanket promotions began, and by the end of the reign the court was full of officials in scarlet.

sentences.zh: 時大赦，惟長流人不聽還，李義府憂憤發病卒。

translations.literal: At the time of the great amnesty, only those sentenced to distant exile were not permitted to return; Li Yifu, aggrieved and enraged, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the general amnesty, only those sentenced to distant exile were barred from return; Li Yifu, aggrieved and enraged, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 自義府流竄，朝士日憂其復入，及聞其卒，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: Since Yifu had been exiled, court officials daily feared his return; when they heard of his death, people's minds were at last eased.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Yifu was exiled, court officials had daily feared his return; when they heard he was dead, the court was finally at ease.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，車駕發泰山；

translations.literal: On bingxu, the imperial carriage departed Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the emperor departed Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，至曲阜，贈孔子太師，以少牢致祭。

translations.literal: On xinmao, he reached Qufu, posthumously enfeoffed Confucius as Grand Preceptor, and offered the minor sacrificial feast.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, he reached Qufu, posthumously enfeoffed Confucius as Grand Preceptor, and offered the lesser sacrificial feast.

sentences.zh: 癸未，至亳州，謁老君廟，上尊號曰太上玄元皇帝。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he reached Bozhou, visited the temple of Lord Lao, and bestowed the honorific title August Emperor of the Mysterious Primordial.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, he reached Bozhou, visited the temple of Lord Lao, and bestowed the honorific title August Emperor of the Mysterious Primordial.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，至東都，留六日；

translations.literal: On dingchou, he reached the Eastern Capital and stayed six days;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, he reached the Eastern Capital and remained six days;

sentences.zh: 甲申，幸合璧宮；
