translations.literal: On jiashen, he visited the Hebi Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, he visited the Hebi Palace;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，至京師，謁太廟。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiachen, he reached the capital and visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, he reached the capital and paid homage at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，左侍極兼檢校右相陸敦信以老疾辭職，拜大司成，兼左侍極，罷政事。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Left Attendant-in-Chief and Acting Right Chancellor Lu Dunxin resigned citing age and illness; he was appointed Grand Master of Education, retaining Left Attendant-in-Chief, and removed from affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Lu Dunxin, Left Attendant-in-Chief and Acting Right Chancellor, resigned citing age and illness; he was appointed Grand Master of Education while retaining Left Attendant-in-Chief, and was removed from active government.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅，鑄乾封泉寶錢，一當十，俟期年盡廢舊錢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Qianfeng coinage was cast, one piece worth ten, to fully replace old coins after one year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Qianfeng treasure coins were cast, each worth ten old coins, with a plan to retire the old currency entirely after one year.

sentences.zh: 高麗泉蓋蘇文卒，長子男生代為莫離支，初知國政，出巡諸城，使其弟男建、男產知留後事。

translations.literal: In Goguryeo Yeon Gaesomun died; his eldest son Nam succeeded as moura, first handling state affairs; he toured the cities and left his brothers Namgeon and Namsan in charge of affairs behind.
translations.idiomatic: In Goguryeo, Yeon Gaesomun died; his eldest son Nam became moura and first assumed control of state affairs; touring the cities, he left his brothers Namgeon and Namsan to manage affairs in his absence.

sentences.zh: 或謂二弟曰：「男生惡二弟之逼，意欲除之，不如先為計。」

translations.literal: Someone told the two brothers, "Nam resents your pressure and intends to eliminate you—you had better strike first."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the two brothers, "Nam resents your rivalry and means to destroy you—you had better act first."

sentences.zh: 二弟初未之信。

translations.literal: At first the two brothers did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the two brothers did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 又有告男生者曰：「二弟恐兄還奪其權，欲拒兄不納。」

translations.literal: Someone else told Nam, "Your two brothers fear that when you return you will seize their power; they mean to refuse you entry."
translations.idiomatic: Someone else told Nam, "Your two brothers fear that on your return you will seize their power; they plan to shut you out."

sentences.zh: 男生潛遣所親往平壤伺之，二弟收掩，得之，乃以王命召男生。

translations.literal: Nam secretly sent a confidant to Pyongyang to spy; the two brothers arrested and seized him, then summoned Nam by royal order.
translations.idiomatic: Nam secretly sent a confidant to Pyongyang to spy on them; the two brothers arrested the man, then summoned Nam by royal order.

sentences.zh: 男生懼，不敢歸；

translations.literal: Nam was afraid and dared not return;
translations.idiomatic: Nam was afraid and dared not return;

sentences.zh: 男建自為莫離支，發兵討之。

translations.literal: Namgeon made himself moura and sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Namgeon declared himself moura and sent troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 男生走保別城，使其子獻誠詣闕求救。

translations.literal: Nam fled to hold another city and sent his son Heonseong to the court to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Nam fled to a fortified city and sent his son Heonseong to the capital to beg for rescue.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬寅，以右驍衛大將軍契苾何力為遼東道安撫大使，將兵救之；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renyin, Qibi Heli, Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, was made Pacification Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit and sent with troops to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renyin, Qibi Heli, Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit and sent with troops to rescue him;

sentences.zh: 以獻誠為右武衛將軍，使為鄉導。

translations.literal: Heonseong was made General of the Right Wuwei Guard and served as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Heonseong was appointed General of the Right Wuwei Guard and assigned as guide.

sentences.zh: 又以右金吾衛將軍龐同善、營州都督高侃為行軍總管，同討高麗。

translations.literal: Pang Tongshan, General of the Right Jinwu Guard, and Gao Kan, Governor of Yingzhou, were also made campaign generals to attack Goguryeo together.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan, General of the Right Jinwu Guard, and Gao Kan, Governor of Yingzhou, were also appointed campaign generals to join the attack on Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙丑朔，徙殷王旭輪為豫王。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, new moon of yichou, Prince Yin Xulun was moved to Prince of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of yichou, Prince Yin Xulun was redesignated Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 以大司憲兼檢校太子左中護劉仁軌為右相。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui, Grand Censor and Acting Left Central Guard of the Heir Apparent, was made Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui, Grand Censor and Acting Left Central Guard of the Heir Apparent, was appointed Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，仁軌為給事中，按畢正義事，李義府怨之，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rengui was a palace secretary investigating Bi Zhengyi's case, Li Yifu resented him and had him sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Rengui was a palace secretary investigating Bi Zhengyi's case, Li Yifu resented him and had him posted as Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會討百濟，仁軌當浮海運糧，時未可行，義府督之，遭風失船，丁夫溺死甚眾，命監察御史袁異式往鞫之。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Baekje came, Rengui was to transport grain by sea; the season was not yet suitable but Yifu pressed him; storms wrecked ships and many laborers drowned; the emperor ordered Supervising Censor Yuan Yishi to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Baekje, Rengui was assigned to transport grain by sea; though the season was unsuitable, Yifu pressed him on; storms wrecked the ships and many laborers drowned; the emperor ordered Supervising Censor Yuan Yishi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 義府謂異式曰：「君能辦事，勿憂無官。」

translations.literal: Yifu told Yishi, "If you can handle this matter, do not worry about lacking office."
translations.idiomatic: Yifu told Yishi, "Handle this well and you need not worry about office."

sentences.zh: 異式至，謂仁軌曰：「君與朝廷何人為仇，宜早自為計。」

translations.literal: When Yishi arrived, he told Rengui, "With whom in court do you have a feud? You should make plans early."
translations.idiomatic: When Yishi arrived, he told Rengui, "Who in court is your enemy? You had better look to yourself."

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「仁軌當官不職，國有常刑，公以法斃之，無所逃命。

translations.literal: Rengui said, "Rengui failed in office; the state has fixed punishments—execute me by law; I have nowhere to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui said, "I failed in office; the state has fixed punishments—execute me by law and I shall not flee.

sentences.zh: 若使遽自引決以快仇人，竊所未甘！」

translations.literal: But to hasten my own death to please an enemy—that I am not willing!"
translations.idiomatic: But to kill myself simply to please an enemy—that I am not willing!"

sentences.zh: 乃具獄以聞。

translations.literal: He then prepared the full case report and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He then prepared the full report and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 異式將行，仍自掣其鎖。

translations.literal: As Yishi was about to leave, he personally removed Rengui's shackles.
translations.idiomatic: As Yishi was about to depart, he personally removed Rengui's shackles.

sentences.zh: 獄上，義府言於上曰：「不斬仁軌，無以謝百姓。」

translations.literal: When the case reached the throne, Yifu told the emperor, "If Rengui is not beheaded, there is no way to answer the people."
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the throne, Yifu told the emperor, "Unless Rengui is beheaded, there is no way to answer the people."

sentences.zh: 舍人源直心曰：「海風暴起，非人力所及。」

translations.literal: Attendant Yuan Zhixin said, "Sea storms arise—beyond human power to control."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Yuan Zhixin said, "Sea storms arise—no human power can control them."

sentences.zh: 上乃命除名，以白衣從軍自效。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Rengui's name removed from registers and sent him to serve in the army as a commoner to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then struck Rengui's name from the registers and ordered him to serve in the army as a commoner to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 義府又諷劉仁願使害之，仁願不忍殺。

translations.literal: Yifu also hinted to Liu Rengyuan to have him killed; Rengyuan could not bear to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also hinted to Liu Rengyuan that he should have Rengui killed; Rengyuan could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 及為大司憲，異式懼，不自安，仁軌瀝觴告之曰：「仁軌若念疇昔之事，有如此觴！」

translations.literal: When Rengui became Grand Censor, Yishi was afraid and ill at ease; Rengui poured out a cup and said, "If Rengui still minded past affairs, there would be such a cup!"
translations.idiomatic: When Rengui became Grand Censor, Yishi was afraid and ill at ease; Rengui drained a cup and said, "If I still bore a grudge over the past, let it be like this cup!"

sentences.zh: 仁軌既知政事，異式尋遷詹事丞；

translations.literal: Once Rengui was in charge of government, Yishi was soon promoted to Assistant to the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Once Rengui took charge of government, Yishi was soon promoted to Assistant to the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 時論紛然，仁軌聞之，遽薦為司元大夫。

translations.literal: Public opinion was divided; when Rengui heard, he quickly recommended him as Chief Director of the Ministry of Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion was divided; when Rengui heard of it, he quickly recommended Yishi for Chief Director of the Ministry of Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 監察御史杜易簡謂人曰：「斯所謂矯枉過正矣！」

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Du Yijian said to others, "This is what they call overcorrecting!"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Du Yijian said to others, "This is what they call overcorrecting!"

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，司元太常伯兼檢校左相竇德玄薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, Dou Dexuan, Minister of Rites and Acting Left Chancellor, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinchou, Dou Dexuan, Minister of Rites and Acting Left Chancellor, died.

sentences.zh: 初，武士擭娶相里氏，生男元慶、元爽；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Shihuo married the Xiangli clan and had sons Yuansing and Yuanshuang;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu Shihuo married a woman of the Xiangli clan and had sons Yuansing and Yuanshuang;

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女，長適越王府法曹賀蘭越石，次皇后，次適郭孝慎。

translations.literal: He also married the Yang clan and had three daughters; the eldest married Helan Yueshi, legal officer of the Prince of Yue's household; the second became empress; the third married Guo Xiaoshen.
translations.idiomatic: He also married a woman of the Yang clan and had three daughters; the eldest married Helan Yueshi, legal officer in the household of the Prince of Yue; the second became empress; the third married Guo Xiaoshen.

sentences.zh: 士擭卒，元慶、元爽及士擭兄子惟良、懷運皆不禮於楊氏，楊氏深銜之。

translations.literal: When Shihuo died, Yuansing, Yuanshuang, and Shihuo's brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun all treated Lady Yang disrespectfully; Lady Yang deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shihuo died, Yuansing, Yuanshuang, and Shihuo's nephews Weiliang and Huaiyun all treated Lady Yang with disrespect; Lady Yang deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 越石、孝慎及孝慎妻並早卒，越石妻生敏之及一女而寡。

translations.literal: Yueshi, Xiaoshen, and Xiaoshen's wife all died early; Yueshi's wife bore Minzhi and a daughter and became a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Yueshi, Xiaoshen, and Xiaoshen's wife all died young; Yueshi's wife bore Minzhi and a daughter and was left a widow.

sentences.zh: 后既立，楊氏號榮國夫人，越石妻號韓國夫人，惟良自始州長史超遷司衛少卿，懷運自瀛州長史遷淄州刺史，元慶自右衛郎將為宗正少卿，元爽自安州戶曹累遷少府少監。

translations.literal: Once Empress Wu was established, Lady Yang was titled Lady of Rong; Yueshi's wife was titled Lady of Han; Weiliang was promoted from prefect of Shizhou to Vice Minister of Palace Guards; Huaiyun from prefect of Yingzhou to prefect of Zibo; Yuansing from captain of the Right Guard to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan; Yuanshuang from registrar of Anzhou rose to Vice Director of Palace Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Once Empress Wu was established, Lady Yang was titled Lady of Rong; Yueshi's wife was titled Lady of Han; Weiliang was promoted from prefect of Shizhou to Vice Minister of Palace Guards; Huaiyun from prefect of Yingzhou to prefect of Zibo; Yuansing from captain of the Right Guard to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan; and Yuanshuang rose from registrar of Anzhou to Vice Director of Palace Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 榮國夫人嘗置酒，謂惟良等曰：「頗憶疇昔之事乎？

translations.literal: Lady of Rong once set out wine and said to Weiliang and the others, "Do you remember affairs of old?
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Rong once set out wine and said to Weiliang and the others, "Do you remember how things used to be?

sentences.zh: 今日之榮貴復何如？」

translations.literal: How does today's glory and rank compare?"
translations.idiomatic: How does today's glory and rank compare?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「惟良等幸以功臣子弟，早登宦籍，揣份量才，不求貴達，豈意以皇后之故，曲荷朝恩，夙夜憂懼，不為榮也。」

translations.literal: They replied, "We are fortunate as sons of meritorious ministers to enter official registers early; weighing our measure and talent, we did not seek high advancement—who would have thought that for the empress's sake we would undeservedly receive court favor? We worry day and night—it is no honor."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We were fortunate as sons of meritorious ministers to enter office early; knowing our measure and talent, we sought no high advancement—who would have thought that for the empress's sake we would receive such undeserved favor from the court? We worry day and night; it is no honor to us."

sentences.zh: 榮國不悅。

translations.literal: Lady of Rong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Rong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 皇后乃上疏，請出惟良等為遠州刺史，外示廉抑，實惡之也。

translations.literal: The empress submitted a memorial asking that Weiliang and the others be sent out as prefects of distant prefectures—outwardly showing restraint, but in fact because she hated them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress submitted a memorial asking that Weiliang and the others be posted as prefects of distant prefectures—outwardly showing restraint, but in truth because she hated them.

sentences.zh: 於是以惟良檢校始州刺史，元慶為龍州刺史，元爽為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiliang was made acting prefect of Shizhou, Yuansing prefect of Longzhou, and Yuanshuang prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weiliang was appointed acting prefect of Shizhou, Yuansing prefect of Longzhou, and Yuanshuang prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 元慶至州，以憂卒。

translations.literal: Yuansing reached his prefecture and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansing reached his prefecture and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 元爽坐事流振州而死。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang was banished to Zhenzhou for an offense and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang was banished to Zhenzhou for an offense and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 韓國夫人及其女以后故出入禁中，皆得幸於上。

translations.literal: The Lady of Han and her daughter, because of Empress Wu, entered and left the inner palace and both found favor with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Han and her daughter, because of Empress Wu, came and went within the inner palace and both found favor with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 韓國尋卒，其女賜號魏國夫人。

translations.literal: Lady of Han soon died; her daughter was granted the title Lady of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Han soon died; her daughter was granted the title Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 上欲以魏國為內職，心難后，未決，后惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make the Lady of Wei an inner consort; his heart found it hard toward Empress Wu, and he could not decide; Empress Wu hated her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make the Lady of Wei an inner consort; he hesitated out of regard for Empress Wu and could not decide; Empress Wu hated her.

sentences.zh: 會惟良、懷運與諸州刺史詣泰山朝覲，從至京師，惟良等獻食。

translations.literal: It happened that Weiliang, Huaiyun, and various prefects came to Mount Tai for the imperial audience, followed to the capital, and Weiliang and the others presented food offerings.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Weiliang, Huaiyun, and various prefects came to Mount Tai for the imperial audience, followed the emperor to the capital, and Weiliang and the others presented food offerings.

sentences.zh: 后密置毒醢中，使魏國食之，暴卒，因歸罪於惟良、懷運，丁未，誅之，改其姓為蝮式。

translations.literal: Empress Wu secretly placed poison in the meat paste, had the Lady of Wei eat it, and she died suddenly; then she blamed Weiliang and Huaiyun; on dingwei they were executed and their surname changed to Fu-shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu secretly placed poison in the meat paste and had the Lady of Wei eat it; she died suddenly. Empress Wu then blamed Weiliang and Huaiyun; on dingwei they were executed and their surname was changed to Fu, "viper."

sentences.zh: 懷運兄懷亮早卒，其妻善氏尤不禮於榮國，坐惟良等沒入掖庭，榮國令後以他事束棘鞭之，肉盡見骨而死。

translations.literal: Huaiyun's elder brother Huailiang died early; his wife Lady Shan especially disrespected Lady of Rong; implicated with Weiliang's case she was seized into the palace women quarters; Lady of Rong ordered the empress to whip her with thorn-bound rods on another pretext until flesh was gone and bone showed, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyun's elder brother Huailiang had died early; his wife Lady Shan had especially disrespected Lady of Rong; implicated in Weiliang's case she was seized into the palace women quarters; Lady of Rong had Empress Wu whip her with thorn-bound rods on another pretext until flesh was stripped to the bone, and she died.

sentences.zh: 九月，龐同善大破高麗兵，泉男生帥眾與同善合。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Pang Tongshan heavily defeated Goguryeo troops; Yeon Nam led his forces to join Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Pang Tongshan routed the Goguryeo army; Yeon Nam led his forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 詔以男生為特進、遼東大都督，兼平壤道安撫大使，封玄菟郡公。

translations.literal: An edict made Nam Special Emissary, Grand Governor of Liaodong, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the Pyongyang Circuit, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xuantu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Nam Special Emissary and Grand Governor of Liaodong, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the Pyongyang Circuit, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xuantu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 戊子，金紫光祿大夫致仕廣平宣公劉祥道薨，子齊賢嗣，齊賢為人方正，上甚重之，為晉州司馬。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Liu Xiangdao, retired Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Duke Xuan of Guangping, died; his son Qixian succeeded; Qixian was upright in character and the emperor greatly valued him; he was Military Assistant of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Liu Xiangdao, retired Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Duke Xuan of Guangping, died; his son Qixian succeeded him; Qixian was upright in character and greatly valued by the emperor; he served as Military Assistant of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 將軍史興宗嘗從上獵苑中，因言晉州產佳鷂，劉齊賢今為司馬，請使捕之。

translations.literal: General Shi Xingzong once accompanied the emperor hunting in the park and mentioned that Jinzhou produced fine hawks; Liu Qixian was now military assistant and he asked that he be sent to catch them.
translations.idiomatic: General Shi Xingzong once accompanied the emperor hunting in the park and remarked that Jinzhou produced fine hawks; Liu Qixian was now military assistant there, and he asked that Qixian be sent to catch them.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「劉齊賢豈捕鷂者邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Is Liu Qixian a hawk-catcher?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is Liu Qixian a hawk-catcher?

sentences.zh: 卿何以此待之！」

translations.literal: Why do you treat him this way!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you treat him this way!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，己酉，以李勣為遼東道行軍大總管兼安撫大使，以司列少常伯安陸郝處俊副之，以擊高麗。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, on jiyou, Li Ji was made Grand Campaign General and Pacification Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit; Hao Chujun of Anlu, Junior Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made his deputy, to attack Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on jiyou, Li Ji was appointed Grand Campaign General and Pacification Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit; Hao Chujun of Anlu, Junior Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed his deputy to attack Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 龐同善、契苾何力並為遼東道行軍副大總管兼安撫大使如故；

translations.literal: Pang Tongshan and Qibi Heli remained Deputy Grand Campaign Generals and Pacification Commissioners of the Liaodong Circuit as before;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan and Qibi Heli remained Deputy Grand Campaign Generals and Pacification Commissioners of the Liaodong Circuit as before;

sentences.zh: 其水陸諸軍總管並運糧使竇義積、獨孤卿雲、郭待封等，並受勣處分。

translations.literal: All army generals by land and sea and grain transport commissioners such as Dou Yiji, Dugu Qingyun, Guo Daifeng, and others were all subject to Li Ji's and Hao Chujun's orders.
translations.idiomatic: All land and sea army generals and grain transport commissioners, including Dou Yiji, Dugu Qingyun, and Guo Daifeng, were placed under Li Ji's and Hao Chujun's command.

sentences.zh: 河北諸州租賦悉詣遼東給軍用。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies from all Hebei prefectures were all sent to Liaodong to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and levies from all Hebei prefectures were directed to Liaodong to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 待封，孝恪之子也。

translations.literal: Daifeng was a son of Xiaoke.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng was Xiaoke's son.

sentences.zh: 勣欲與其婿京兆杜懷恭偕行，以求勳效。

translations.literal: Ji wished to travel together with his son-in-law Du Huaigong of Jingzhao, seeking merit for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji wanted his son-in-law Du Huaigong of Jingzhao to accompany him on campaign, hoping thereby to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 懷恭辭以貧，勣贍之；

translations.literal: Huaigong declined on grounds of poverty, and Ji supplied him;
translations.idiomatic: Huaigong pleaded poverty, and Li Ji provided for him;

sentences.zh: 復辭以無奴馬，又贍之。

translations.literal: Again he declined on grounds of having no servants or horses, and Ji again supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again, saying he had no servants or horses, and Li Ji supplied him once more.

sentences.zh: 懷恭辭窮，乃亡匿岐陽山中，謂人曰：「公欲以我立法耳。」

translations.literal: Huaigong having exhausted his excuses, he fled and hid in the mountains of Qiyang, saying to people, "The Duke means to make me a legal precedent."
translations.idiomatic: With his excuses exhausted, Huaigong fled and hid in the Qiyang mountains, telling people, "The Duke wants to use me to set an example under the law."

sentences.zh: 勣聞之，流涕曰：「杜郎疏放，此或有之。」

translations.literal: When Ji heard this, he wept and said, "Young Du is free and unrestrained—this may be so."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Li Ji wept and said, "Young Du is careless and free-spirited—that much may be true."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He then let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上耕籍田，有司進耒耜，加以雕飾。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor plowed the sacred field; the responsible officials presented plow and rake ornamented with carving.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field; the officials presented plow and rake lavishly decorated.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「耒耜農夫所執，豈宜如此之麗！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Plow and rake are what farmers hold—how can they be so splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These are the tools farmers use—how can they be made so ornate!"

sentences.zh: 命易之。

translations.literal: He ordered them replaced.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them exchanged for plain ones.

sentences.zh: 既而耕之，九推乃止。

translations.literal: Then he plowed, and after nine pushes stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He then plowed until he had made nine furrows and stopped.

sentences.zh: 自行乾封泉寶錢，穀帛踴貴，商賈不行，癸未，詔罷之。

translations.literal: Since the Qianfeng Quanbao coins were issued, grain and cloth soared in price and merchants ceased trading; on guimwei, an edict abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianfeng Quanbao coin was introduced, grain and cloth prices soared and commerce stalled; on guimwei, an edict abolished the currency.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁酉，涪陵悼王愔薨。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingyou, Prince Dao of Fuling, Yin, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingyou, Prince Dao of Fuling, Yin, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，復以萬年宮為九成宮。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Wannian Palace was again renamed Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Wannian Palace was restored to the name Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 生羌十二州為吐蕃所破，三月，戊寅，悉廢之。

translations.literal: The twelve Shengqiang prefectures had been broken by Tibet; in the third month, on wuyin, all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Shengqiang prefectures had been overrun by Tibet; in the third month, on wuyin, they were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 上屢責侍臣不進賢，眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly reproached his attendants for not recommending the worthy, and none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly rebuked his courtiers for failing to recommend able men, and no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 司列少常伯李安期對曰：「天下未嘗無賢，亦非群臣敢蔽賢也。

translations.literal: Li Anqi, Vice Director of Rankings and Second Grand Master of the Presiding Office, replied, "Under Heaven there has never been a lack of worthies, nor have the ministers dared to hide the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anqi, Vice Director of Rankings and Second Grand Master of the Presiding Office, replied, "The realm has never lacked worthy men, and it is not that ministers dare conceal talent.

sentences.zh: 比來公卿有所薦引，為讒者已指為朋黨，滯淹者未獲伸，而在位者先獲罪矣，是以各各杜口耳。

translations.literal: Lately when high officials have made recommendations, slanderers have already denounced them as faction-mates; those long held back have not had their turn, while those in office have first been punished—therefore each has sealed his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, whenever high officials have recommended someone, calumniators have at once cried "faction"; men long passed over never get their chance, while those already in office are punished first—so everyone keeps silent.

sentences.zh: 陛下果推至誠以待之，其誰不願舉所知！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly extends utmost sincerity in treating them, who would not wish to recommend those he knows!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly treats us with complete sincerity, who would not gladly recommend those he knows!

sentences.zh: 此在陛下，非在群臣也。」

translations.literal: This lies with Your Majesty, not with the ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The remedy lies with Your Majesty, not with the ministers."

sentences.zh: 上深以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 安期，百藥之子也。

translations.literal: Anqi was a son of Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi was Baiyao's son.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，西台侍郎楊弘武、戴至德、正諫大夫兼東台侍郎李安期、東台舍人昌樂張文瓘、司列少常伯兼正諫大夫河北趙仁本並同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Vice Director Yang Hongwu of the Western Office, Dai Zhide, Remonstrating Grandee and Vice Director Li Anqi of the Eastern Office, Eastern Office Aide Zhang Wenjun of Changle, and Vice Director of Rankings and Remonstrating Grandee Zhao Renben of Hebei were all made Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Yang Hongwu, Vice Director of the Western Office; Dai Zhide; Li Anqi, Remonstrating Grandee and Vice Director of the Eastern Office; Zhang Wenjun of Changle, Aide of the Eastern Office; and Zhao Renben of Hebei, Vice Director of Rankings and Remonstrating Grandee, were all appointed Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 弘武，素之弟子；

translations.literal: Hongwu was a disciple of Su;
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu was a disciple of Su.

sentences.zh: 至德，冑之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhide was a nephew of Zhou's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide was Zhou's nephew.

sentences.zh: 時造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，頻征伐四夷，廄馬萬匹，倉庫漸虛，張文瓘諫曰：「隋鑒不遠，願勿使百姓生怨。」

translations.literal: At the time Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi, and other palaces were being built, campaigns against the four border peoples were frequent, stable horses numbered ten thousand, and the granaries grew empty; Zhang Wenjun remonstrated, "Sui's warning is not distant—I pray that the people not be made to harbor resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Palaces such as Penglai, Shangyang, and Hebi were under construction, campaigns against the frontier peoples were constant, the stables held ten thousand horses, and the treasury ran low; Zhang Wenjun remonstrated, "The Sui collapse is a recent lesson—do not give the people cause for resentment."

sentences.zh: 上納其言，減廄馬數千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and reduced stable horses by several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice and cut several thousand horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，己丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day jichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the new moon of jichou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，東台侍郎同東西台三品李安期出為荊州長史。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Li Anqi, Vice Director of the Eastern Office and Third Rank Associate of Both Offices, was sent out as prefectural chief of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Li Anqi, Vice Director of the Eastern Office and Third Rank Associate of Both Offices, was assigned as chief administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚申，上以久疾，命太子弘監國。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengshen, because of long illness the emperor ordered Crown Prince Hong to supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengshen, the emperor, long ill, ordered Crown Prince Hong to oversee the government.

sentences.zh: 辛未，李勣拔高麗之新城，使契苾何力守之。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Li Ji captured Xincheng of Goguryeo and had Qibi Heli garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Li Ji took Goguryeo's Xincheng and left Qibi Heli to hold it.

sentences.zh: 勣初度遼，謂諸將曰：「新城，高麗西邊要害，不先得之，餘城未易取也。」

translations.literal: When Ji first crossed the Liao, he told the generals, "Xincheng is the key point on Goguryeo's western border; if we do not take it first, the other cities will not be easy to capture."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ji first crossed the Liao River, he told his generals, "Xincheng is the vital stronghold on Goguryeo's western frontier; unless we seize it first, the other cities will be hard to take."

sentences.zh: 遂攻之，城人師夫仇等縛城主開門降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked it; the townsman Shifuchou and others bound the city commander and opened the gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked it; Shifuchou and others in the city bound the garrison commander and opened the gates in surrender.

sentences.zh: 勣引兵進擊，一十六城皆下之。

translations.literal: Ji led troops forward in attack and took all sixteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji pressed the attack and captured sixteen cities.

sentences.zh: 龐同善、高侃尚在新城，泉男建遣兵襲其營，左武衛將軍薛仁貴擊破之。

translations.literal: Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan were still at Xincheng; Yeon Gaemun sent troops to raid their camp, and Left Martial Guard General Xue Rengui routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan were still at Xincheng when Yeon Gaemun sent troops to strike their camp; Xue Rengui, General of the Left Martial Guard, defeated them.

sentences.zh: 侃進至金山，與高麗戰，不利，高麗乘勝逐北，仁貴引兵橫擊之，大破高麗，斬首五萬餘級，拔南蘇、木底、蒼巖三城，與泉男生軍合。

translations.literal: Kan advanced to Jinshan and fought Goguryeo with an unfavorable outcome; Goguryeo pursued in victory, and Rengui led troops in a flanking strike, routing Goguryeo greatly, beheading more than fifty thousand, capturing the three cities Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan, and joining Yeon Namsa's army.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan advanced to Jinshan and fought Goguryeo without success; as the enemy pressed their advantage in pursuit, Rengui struck them from the flank, crushing the Goguryeo force, taking more than fifty thousand heads, capturing Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan, and linking up with Yeon Namsa's army.

sentences.zh: 郭待封以水軍自別道趣平壤，勣遣別將馮師本載糧仗以資之。

translations.literal: Guo Daifeng led the navy by a separate route toward Pyongyang; Ji sent separate commander Feng Shiben to carry grain and weapons to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Daifeng led the naval force by a separate route toward Pyongyang; Li Ji sent the subordinate commander Feng Shiben with grain and arms to resupply him.

sentences.zh: 師本船破，失期，待封軍中饑窘，欲作書與勣，恐為虜所得，知其虛實，乃作離合詩以與勣。

translations.literal: Shiben's ships were wrecked and he missed the rendezvous; Daifeng's army was hungry and distressed; wishing to write to Ji, he feared the enemy might capture it and learn his true state—so he sent a disjoined-character poem to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shiben's ships were wrecked and he failed to arrive on time; Daifeng's troops were starving; wanting to write Li Ji but fearing capture by the enemy would reveal his weakness, he sent a cryptogram poem instead.

sentences.zh: 勣怒曰：「軍事方急，何以詩為？

translations.literal: Ji angrily said, "Military affairs are urgent—why send a poem?
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji fumed, "The crisis is acute—what is the use of poetry?

sentences.zh: 必斬之！」

translations.literal: He must be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He must be executed!"

sentences.zh: 行軍管記通事舍人河南元萬頃為釋其義，勣乃更遣糧仗赴之。

translations.literal: Campaign scribe and Interpreter-in-Attendance Yuan Wanqing of Henan explained its meaning, and Ji then sent grain and weapons again to his relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wanqing of Henan, campaign secretary and Interpreter-in-Attendance, decoded the message, and Li Ji then dispatched fresh supplies.

sentences.zh: 萬頃作《檄高麗文》，曰「不知守鴨綠之險。」

translations.literal: Wanqing composed a "Proclamation Against Goguryeo" saying, "They do not know to hold the peril of the Yalu."
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing drafted a proclamation against Goguryeo declaring, "The enemy does not know enough to defend the Yalu crossing."

sentences.zh: 泉男建報曰：「謹聞命矣！」

translations.literal: Yeon Gaemun replied, "I have respectfully received the command!"
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaemun answered, "Your instruction is respectfully noted!"

sentences.zh: 即移兵據鴨綠津，唐兵不得渡。

translations.literal: He immediately shifted troops to hold Yalu Ford, and Tang troops could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: He at once moved his troops to occupy the Yalu crossing, and the Tang army could not ford the river.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，流萬頃於嶺南。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he banished Wanqing to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the emperor exiled Wanqing to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 郝處俊在高麗城下，未及成列，高麗奄至，軍中大駭。

translations.literal: Hao Chujun was below a Goguryeo city; before the ranks were formed, Goguryeo suddenly arrived, and the army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Below a Goguryeo city, Hao Chujun had not yet formed his battle line when the enemy suddenly appeared, throwing the army into panic.

sentences.zh: 處俊據胡床，方食干□，潛簡精銳，擊敗之，將士服其膽略。

translations.literal: Chujun sat on a folding stool, was just eating dried provisions, secretly picked elite troops, defeated them, and officers and soldiers admired his daring and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun remained seated on his camp stool, still eating dried rations, quietly selected crack troops, and routed the enemy; the men marveled at his courage and composure.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，甲午，詔：「自今祀昊天上帝、五帝、皇地示氏、神州地示氏，並以高祖、太宗配，仍合祀昊天上帝、五帝於明堂。」

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on jiawu, an edict said, "From now on in sacrificing to Grand Heaven, the Five Emperors, the August Earth-spirit, and the Spirit of the Central Land of the Nine Regions, let Gaozu and Taizong be associated; and Grand Heaven and the Five Emperors shall still be jointly worshipped in the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on jiawu, an edict declared, "Henceforth in rites to Heaven, the Five Emperors, the supreme Earth deity, and the regional Earth deities of the central realm, Gaozu and Taizong shall serve as associates; Heaven and the Five Emperors shall still be worshipped together in the Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 是歲，海南獠陷瓊州。

translations.literal: That year, the Hainan Liao seized Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Liao tribes of Hainan overran Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬下，以右相劉仁軌為遼東道副大總管。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renzi, Right Chancellor Liu Ren'gui was made Deputy Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renzi, Right Chancellor Liu Ren'gui was appointed deputy grand commander of the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，李勣等拔高麗扶餘城。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renwu, Li Ji and others captured Fuyu city of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu, Li Ji and his forces took Goguryeo's Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 薛仁貴既破高麗於金山，乘勝將三千人將攻扶餘城，諸將以其兵少，止之。

translations.literal: After Xue Rengui had routed Goguryeo at Jinshan, he pressed the victory with three thousand men to attack Fuyu city; the generals, because his force was small, stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Rengui's victory over Goguryeo at Jinshan, he pressed on with three thousand men to attack Fuyu; the other generals, thinking his force too small, tried to hold him back.

sentences.zh: 仁貴曰：「兵不必多，顧用之何如耳。」

translations.literal: Rengui said, "Troops need not be many—it depends on how they are used."
translations.idiomatic: Rengui said, "Numbers are not what matter—it is how the troops are used."

sentences.zh: 遂為前鋒以進，與高麗戰，大破之，殺獲萬餘人，遂拔扶餘城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he served as vanguard and advanced, fought Goguryeo, routed them greatly, killed and captured more than ten thousand, and then took Fuyu city.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the vanguard forward, crushed the Goguryeo force, killing and capturing more than ten thousand, and took Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 扶餘川中四十餘城皆望風請服。

translations.literal: More than forty cities in the Fuyu River region all submitted at the mere report of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty cities along the Fuyu River submitted at the first news of his advance.

sentences.zh: 侍御史洛陽賈言忠奉使自遼東還，上問以軍事，言忠對曰：「高麗必平。」

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Jia Yanzhong of Luoyang, returning from a mission in Liaodong, was questioned by the emperor about military affairs; Yanzhong replied, "Goguryeo will certainly be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yanzhong of Luoyang, a supervising censor returning from a mission in Liaodong, was asked about the campaign; he replied, "Goguryeo is sure to fall."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿何以知之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How can you be so sure?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「隋煬帝東征而不克者，人心離怨故也；

translations.literal: He replied, "Emperor Yang of Sui failed in his eastern campaigns because the people's hearts were alienated and resentful;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Emperor Yang of Sui failed in the east because the people had turned against him;

sentences.zh: 先帝東征而不克者，高麗未有釁也。

translations.literal: the former emperor's eastern campaigns failed because Goguryeo had not yet split.
translations.idiomatic: the former emperor's eastern campaigns failed because Goguryeo had not yet been torn by internal strife.

sentences.zh: 今高藏微弱，權臣擅命，蓋蘇文死，男建兄弟內相攻奪，男生傾心內附，為我鄉導，彼之情偽，靡不知之。

translations.literal: Now Gao Zang is weak, powerful ministers act on their own authority, Gaisuwen is dead, the brothers Gaemun contend within for power, Namsa has turned his heart inward to submit and serves as our guide—their true and false conditions are all known to us.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gao Zang is weak, power rests with usurping ministers, Gaisuwen is dead, Gaemun and his brothers are fighting among themselves, and Namsa has come over to our side as a guide—we know their situation inside and out.

sentences.zh: 以陛下明聖，國家富強，將士盡力，以乘高麗之亂，其勢必克，不俟再舉矣。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's brilliance and sagacity, the state's wealth and strength, and officers and soldiers giving their full effort, to seize Goguryeo's disorder—the outcome must be victory, without waiting for a second campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's wisdom, the realm's strength, and the army fighting at full pitch, victory over Goguryeo in its present turmoil is certain—there will be no need for a second campaign.

sentences.zh: 且高麗連年饑饉，妖異屢降，人心危駭，其亡可翹足待也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Goguryeo has suffered famine year after year, strange portents have repeatedly appeared, and people's hearts are fearful and alarmed—its fall can be awaited with a lifted foot."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Goguryeo has endured famine year after year, omens have multiplied, and the people live in dread—its collapse can be awaited with folded arms."

sentences.zh: 上又問：「遼東諸將孰賢？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked, "Which of the Liaodong generals is most worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Which of the generals in Liaodong is the best?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「薛仁貴勇冠三軍；

translations.literal: He replied, "Xue Rengui's courage leads the whole army;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Xue Rengui's courage is unmatched in the army;

sentences.zh: 龐同善雖不善鬥，而持軍嚴整；

translations.literal: Pang Tongshan, though not skilled in combat, keeps his army strict and orderly;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan is not the boldest fighter, but he keeps his troops in tight order;

sentences.zh: 高侃勤儉自處，忠果有謀；

translations.literal: Gao Kan is frugal in his personal conduct, loyal, resolute, and resourceful;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan lives frugally, and is loyal, resolute, and shrewd;

sentences.zh: 契苾何力沉毅能斷，雖頗忌前，而有統御之才；

translations.literal: Qibi Heli is steady and resolute and can decide; though somewhat given to old resentments, he has talent for command;
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli is steady and decisive; though he still bears old grudges, he has real command ability;

sentences.zh: 然夙夜小心，忘身憂國，皆莫及李勣也。」

translations.literal: yet in vigilance day and night, forgetting self and worrying for the state, none can match Li Ji."
translations.idiomatic: but in tireless care for the state and readiness to risk himself, none can equal Li Ji."

sentences.zh: 上深然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply convinced by his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 泉男建復遣兵五萬人救扶餘城，與李勣等遇於薛賀水，合戰，大破之，斬獲三萬餘人，進攻大行城，拔之。

translations.literal: Yeon Gaemun again sent fifty thousand troops to relieve Fuyu city; they met Li Ji and others at the Xuehe River, joined battle, and were routed greatly; more than thirty thousand were beheaded or captured; they advanced to attack Daxing city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaemun sent another fifty thousand men to relieve Fuyu; they met Li Ji's force at the Xuehe River and were crushed, with more than thirty thousand killed or captured; the Tang army then advanced on Daxing and took it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議明堂制度略定，三月，庚寅，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Court discussion of Bright Hall ritual regulations was largely settled; in the third month, on gengyin, there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Once court debate over Bright Hall ritual had largely been settled, in the third month, on gengyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the emperor went to Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，彗星見於五車。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingchen, a comet appeared in the constellation Wuche.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingchen, a comet appeared in the Five Chariots constellation.

sentences.zh: 上避正殿，減常膳，撤樂。

translations.literal: The emperor avoided the main hall, reduced his regular meals, and removed music.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the main hall, cut back his meals, and suspended music.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗等奏請復常，曰：「彗見東北，高麗將滅之兆也。」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong and others memorialized asking to resume normal rites, saying, "The comet in the northeast is an omen that Goguryeo will perish."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong and others memorialized asking to resume normal court practice, saying, "The comet in the northeast foretells Goguryeo's fall."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕之不德，謫見於天，豈可歸咎小夷！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "My lack of virtue has brought reproof from Heaven—how can I lay blame on a petty border people!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Heaven rebukes me for my failings—how can I shift the blame onto a petty frontier state!

sentences.zh: 且高麗百姓，亦朕之百姓也。」

translations.literal: Moreover the people of Goguryeo are also my people."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the people of Goguryeo are my people too."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，彗星見。

translations.literal: On wuchen, a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the comet appeared again.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，西台侍郎、同東西台三品楊弘武薨。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Yang Hongwu, Vice Director of the Western Office and Third Rank Associate of Both Offices, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Yang Hongwu, Vice Director of the Western Office and Third Rank Associate of Both Offices, died.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛酉，卑列道行軍總管、右威衛將軍劉仁願坐征高麗逗留，流姚州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Liu Renyuan, campaign commander of the Beilie Route and General of the Right Martial Guard, was punished for delay in the Goguryeo campaign and exiled to Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Liu Renyuan, campaign commander of the Beilie Route and General of the Right Martial Guard, was punished for stalling during the Goguryeo campaign and exiled to Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，李勣拔平壤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi, Li Ji captured Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, Li Ji took Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 勣既克大行城，諸軍出他道者皆與勣會，進至鴨綠柵，高麗發兵拒戰，勣等奮擊，大破之，追奔二百餘里，拔辰夷城，諸城遁逃及降者相繼。

translations.literal: After Ji had taken Daxing city, all armies that had marched by other routes joined Ji; they advanced to Yalu Stockade; Goguryeo sent troops to resist battle; Ji and the others struck fiercely and routed them greatly, pursuing the fleeing enemy more than two hundred li, taking Chenyi city; cities that fled or surrendered followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ji had taken Daxing, the other columns joined him and they advanced to the Yalu stockade; when Goguryeo troops came out to fight, Li Ji drove them back in a crushing victory, pursuing them more than two hundred li, taking Chenyi, and watching city after city flee or surrender.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力先引兵至平壤城下，勣軍繼之，圍平壤月餘，高麗王藏遣泉男產帥首領九十八人，持白幡詣勣降，勣以禮接之。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli first led troops to below Pyongyang city; Ji's army followed; they besieged Pyongyang for more than a month; King Zang of Goguryeo sent Yeon Namchan leading ninety-eight chieftains with white banners to Ji to surrender, and Ji received them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli reached Pyongyang first, Li Ji's army followed, and the siege lasted more than a month; King Zang of Goguryeo sent Yeon Namchan with ninety-eight chieftains bearing white banners to surrender to Li Ji, who received them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 泉男建猶閉門拒守，頻遣兵出戰，皆敗。

translations.literal: Yeon Gaemun still shut the gates and held out, repeatedly sending troops out to fight, and all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaemun still held the gates shut and sent troops out again and again, but each sortie was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 男建以軍事委僧信誠，信誠密遣人詣勣，請為內應。

translations.literal: Gaemun entrusted military affairs to the monk Sinseong; Sinseong secretly sent someone to Ji, asking to serve as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Gaemun entrusted military affairs to the monk Sinseong, who secretly sent a messenger to Li Ji offering to act as an inside agent.

sentences.zh: 後五日，信誠開門，勣縱兵登城鼓噪，焚城四周，男建自刺，不死，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Five days later Sinseong opened the gate; Ji let troops storm the wall with drums and shouts, burned all around the city; Gaemun stabbed himself but did not die, and was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Sinseong opened the gates; Li Ji's men stormed the walls with a great clamor and set fires around the city; Gaemun tried to kill himself but failed, and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 高麗悉平。

translations.literal: Goguryeo was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was completely subdued.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊午，以烏茶國婆羅門盧迦逸多為懷化大將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuwu, the Brahmin Luqayaduo of Udyana was made General of Cherishing Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuwu, Luqayaduo, a Brahmin from Udyana, was made General of Cherishing Transformation.

sentences.zh: 逸多自言能合不死藥，上將餌之。

translations.literal: Yiduo claimed he could compound an elixir of immortality; the emperor was about to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yiduo claimed he could prepare an elixir of immortality, and the emperor was about to ingest it.

sentences.zh: 東台侍郎郝處俊諫曰：「修短有命，非藥可延。

translations.literal: Hao Chujun, Vice Director of the Eastern Office, remonstrated, "Length of life is fated—it cannot be extended by medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chujun, Vice Director of the Eastern Office, remonstrated, "Life and death are ordained—no drug can prolong them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之末，先帝服那羅邇娑婆寐藥，竟無效；

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era the former emperor took the medicine of Narayana Svami, but in the end it had no effect;
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguan era the late emperor took the medicine of Narayana Svami, and it did no good;

sentences.zh: 大漸之際，名醫不知所為，議者歸罪娑婆寐，將加顯戮，恐取笑戎狄而止。

translations.literal: at the point of death eminent physicians did not know what to do; critics blamed Svami and were about to execute him publicly, but stopped for fear of becoming a laughingstock among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: when he was dying the best physicians were helpless; critics blamed Svami and nearly had him executed, but held back for fear of making the court a laughingstock among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 前鑒不遠，願陛下深察。」

translations.literal: The warning precedent is not distant—I pray Your Majesty examine it deeply."
translations.idiomatic: That recent lesson is still before us—I urge Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 李勣將至，上命先以高藏等獻於昭陵，具軍容，奏凱歌，入京師，獻於太廟。

translations.literal: When Li Ji was about to arrive, the emperor ordered that Gao Zang and the others first be presented at Zhaoling with full military array, victory songs performed, then brought into the capital and presented at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Ji reached the capital, the emperor ordered Gao Zang and the other captives presented first at Taizong's tomb with full military ceremony and songs of victory, then brought into the capital and offered at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，上受俘於含元殿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, the emperor received the captives at Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, the emperor received the captives in audience at Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 以高藏政非己出，赦以為司平太常伯、員外同正。

translations.literal: Because Gao Zang's policies had not been of his own making, he was pardoned and made Minister of Balance and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple, supplementary with full concurrent rank.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao Zang had never truly ruled in his own right, he was pardoned and appointed Minister of Balance and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple, with supplementary full concurrent rank.

sentences.zh: 以泉男產為司宰少卿，僧信誠為銀青光祿大夫，泉男生為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Yeon Namchan was made Vice Director of the Chief Steward's Office, Seng Xincheng was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Bearing the Golden Grand Seal, and Yeon Nam was made Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Namchan was appointed Vice Director of the Chief Steward's Office, Seng Xincheng was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Bearing the Golden Grand Seal, and Yeon Nam was appointed Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 李勣以下，封賞有差。

translations.literal: Below Li Ji, rewards and enfeoffments varied by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji and those below him received rewards and enfeoffments in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 泉男建流黔州，扶餘豐流嶺南，分高麗五部、百七十六城、六十九萬餘戶，為九都督府、四十二州、百縣，置安東都護府於平壤以統之。

translations.literal: Yeon Gaemun was exiled to Qianzhou, Buyeo Pung to Lingnan; Goguryeo's five departments, 176 cities, and more than 690,000 households were divided into nine area commands, 42 prefectures, and 100 counties, and the Protectorate-General of the Pacified East was established at Pyongyang to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaemun was banished to Qianzhou and Buyeo Pung to Lingnan; Goguryeo's five departments, 176 cities, and more than 690,000 households were carved into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and a hundred counties, with the Protectorate-General of the Pacified East set up at Pyongyang to rule them.

sentences.zh: 擢其酋帥有功者為都督、刺史、縣令，與華人參理。

translations.literal: Chiefs and leaders who had rendered merit were promoted to be area commissioners, prefects, and county magistrates, administering together with Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious tribal chiefs were promoted to area commissioners, prefects, and county magistrates and governed alongside Han officials.

sentences.zh: 以右威衛大將軍薛仁貴檢校安東都護，總兵二萬人以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Grand General of the Right Mighty Guard Xue Rengui was made acting Protector-General of the Pacified East, commanding 20,000 troops to pacify and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui, Grand General of the Right Mighty Guard, was made acting Protector-General of the Pacified East with twenty thousand troops to pacify and reassure the region.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上祀南郊，告平高麗，以李勣為亞獻。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Altar, announcing the pacification of Goguryeo, with Li Ji as secondary presenter.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar to announce Goguryeo's pacification, with Li Ji as secondary presenter.

sentences.zh: 己巳，謁太廟。

translations.literal: On jisi, he visited the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, he visited the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 渭南尉劉延祐，弱冠登進士第，政事為畿縣最。

translations.literal: Liu Yanyou, magistrate of Weinan, passed the jinshi examination while still in his early twenties; his administration was ranked foremost among the metropolitan districts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanyou, magistrate of Weinan, had passed the jinshi examination before he was twenty, and his administration ranked first among the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 李勣謂之曰：「足下春秋甫爾，遽擅大名，宜稍自貶抑，無為獨出人右也。」

translations.literal: Li Ji said to him, "You are still young in years, yet you have swiftly risen to great renown; you ought to lower yourself a little and not stand alone above others."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji told him, "You are still young, yet you have already won great renown; you should hold yourself back a little and not stand conspicuously above others."

sentences.zh: 時有敕，征遼軍士逃亡，限內不首及首而更逃者，身斬，妻子籍沒。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict: soldiers of the Liaodong campaign who deserted and, within the time limit, did not surrender or, having surrendered, fled again, would be beheaded and their wives and children registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict decreed that soldiers of the Liaodong campaign who deserted and, within the allotted time, failed to surrender—or surrendered and fled again—would be beheaded and their wives and children registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 太子上表，以為：「如此之比，其數至多。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted a memorial, stating, "Cases such as these are extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince submitted a memorial arguing that "cases such as these are extremely numerous.

sentences.zh: 或遇病不及隊伍，怖懼而逃；

translations.literal: Some fell ill and could not keep up with their units, and fled in fear;
translations.idiomatic: Some fell ill and could not keep up with their units and fled in terror;

sentences.zh: 或因樵采為賊所掠；

translations.literal: some were seized by bandits while gathering firewood;
translations.idiomatic: some were seized by bandits while gathering firewood;

sentences.zh: 或渡海漂沒；

translations.literal: some were lost at sea while crossing the ocean;
translations.idiomatic: some were lost at sea crossing the ocean;

sentences.zh: 或深入賊庭，為所傷殺。

translations.literal: some went deep into enemy territory and were wounded or killed.
translations.idiomatic: some went deep into enemy territory and were wounded or killed.

sentences.zh: 軍法嚴重，同隊恐並獲罪，即舉以為逃，軍旅之中，不暇勘當，直據隊司通狀關移所屬，妻子沒官，情實可哀。

translations.literal: Military law was severe; comrades in the same unit, fearing they would be punished together, at once reported them as deserters; in the army there was no time to investigate, and on the mere tally slip from the unit clerk the case was forwarded to the appropriate authority—the men's wives and children were seized by the state, which was truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Military law was harsh; comrades in the same unit, fearing shared punishment, at once reported them as deserters. In camp there was no time to investigate, and on the unit clerk's tally alone the case was forwarded—the men's wives and children were seized by the state, which was truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『與其殺不辜，寧失不經。』

translations.literal: The Documents says, 'Better to err through leniency than to execute the innocent.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'Better to err through leniency than to execute the innocent.'

sentences.zh: 伏願逃亡之家，免其配沒。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray that the families of those who fled be spared registration and confiscation."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that the families of deserters be spared registration and confiscation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司戎太常伯姜恪兼檢校左相，司平太常伯閻立本守右相。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Minister of the Army and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple Jiang Ke was additionally made acting Left Chancellor; Minister of Balance and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple Yan Liben was put in charge as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Jiang Ke, minister of the army and grand master of the grand ancestral temple, was additionally made acting Left Chancellor; Yan Liben, minister of balance and grand master of the grand ancestral temple, was put in charge as Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，京師及山東、江、淮旱、饑。

translations.literal: That year the capital, Shandong, and the Yangzi and Huai regions suffered drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year the capital, Shandong, and the Yangzi and Huai regions suffered drought and famine.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，辛酉，以張文瓘為東台侍郎，以右肅機、檢校太子中護譙人李敬玄為西台侍郎，並同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on xinyou, Zhang Wen'guan was made Vice Director of the Eastern Office; Right Secretariat Attendant and acting Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household Li Jingxuan of Qiao was made Vice Director of the Western Office; both were made Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on xinyou, Zhang Wen'guan was appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Office, and Li Jingxuan of Qiao, right secretariat attendant and acting supervisor of the heir apparent's household, was appointed Vice Director of the Western Office; both were made Third Rank Associates of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 先是同三品不入銜，至是始入銜。

translations.literal: Previously, Third Rank Associates were not entered in the official title line; from this time they were.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Third Rank Associates had not been listed in official titles; from this time they were.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以雍州長史盧承慶為司刑太常伯。

translations.literal: On guihai, Chief Administrator of Yongzhou Lu Chengqing was made Minister of Punishments and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Lu Chengqing, chief administrator of Yongzhou, was appointed Minister of Punishments and Grand Master of the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 承慶嘗考內外官，有一官督運，遭風失米，承慶考之曰：「監運損糧，考中下。」

translations.literal: Chengqing once assessed inner and outer officials; one official supervising transport encountered a storm and lost grain; Chengqing assessed him, saying, "Supervising transport with grain lost—assessment: middle lower."
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing once assessed inner and outer officials; one official supervising transport lost grain in a storm, and Chengqing assessed him, saying, "Supervising transport with grain lost—assessment: middle lower."

sentences.zh: 其人容色自若，無言而退。

translations.literal: That man kept his expression unchanged and withdrew without a word.
translations.idiomatic: The man kept his composure and withdrew without a word.

sentences.zh: 承慶重期雅量，改注曰：「非力所及，考中中。」

translations.literal: Chengqing, greatly impressed by his magnanimity, changed the note to, "Beyond one's power to prevent—assessment: middle grade."
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing, deeply impressed by his composure, changed the note to, "Beyond one's power to prevent—assessment: middle grade."

sentences.zh: 既無喜容，亦無愧詞。

translations.literal: He showed neither joy nor shame in his words.
translations.idiomatic: He showed neither pleasure nor shame.

sentences.zh: 又改曰：「寵辱不驚，考中上。」

translations.literal: He changed it again: "Unmoved by favor or disgrace—assessment: middle upper."
translations.idiomatic: He changed it again: "Unmoved by favor or disgrace—assessment: middle upper."

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌，東台侍郎郝處俊同東、西台三品。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingxu, Eastern Office Vice Director Hao Chujun was made Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingxu, Hao Chujun, vice director of the Eastern Office, was made Third Rank Associate of Both Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔定明堂制度：其基八觚，其宇上圓，覆以清陽玉葉，其門牆階級，窗欞楣柱，柳楶枅栱，皆法天地陰陽律歷之數。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict fixed the Hall of Brightness system: its foundation octagonal, its roof domed, covered with green tiles; its gates, walls, steps, windows, lintels, columns, and bracket sets—all according to the numbers of Heaven and Earth, yin and yang, pitch pipes, and the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, an edict fixed the design of the Hall of Brightness: an octagonal foundation, a domed roof covered with green tiles, and gates, walls, steps, windows, lintels, columns, and bracket sets all proportioned to the numbers of Heaven and Earth, yin and yang, pitch pipes, and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 詔下之後，眾議猶未決，又會饑饉，竟不果立。

translations.literal: After the edict was issued, debate still had not settled the matter; famine also struck, and in the end it was never built.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was issued, debate still had not settled the matter; famine struck as well, and in the end the hall was never built.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己酉朔，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month, jiyou, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day, jiyou, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 高麗之民多離叛者，敕徙高麗戶三萬八千二百於江、淮之南，及山南、京西諸州空曠之地，留其貧弱者，使守安東。

translations.literal: Many Goguryeo people had rebelled and fled; an edict ordered 38,200 Goguryeo households moved south of the Yangzi and Huai, and to vacant lands in the mountain-south and capital-west prefectures; the poor and weak were left behind to hold the Pacified East.
translations.idiomatic: Many Goguryeo people had rebelled and fled; an edict ordered 38,200 Goguryeo households moved south of the Yangzi and Huai and to vacant lands in the mountain-south and capital-west prefectures, while the poor and weak were left behind to hold the Pacified East.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month, wushen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day, wushen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丁未朔，詔以十月幸涼州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day of the month, dingwei, an edict announced that in the tenth month the emperor would visit Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day, dingwei, an edict announced that in the tenth month the emperor would visit Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時隴右虛耗，議者多以為未宜游幸。

translations.literal: At that time Longyou was depleted; most who debated the matter thought a tour inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou was then exhausted, and most who debated the matter thought a tour ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，辛亥，御延福殿，召五品已上謂曰：「自古帝王，莫不巡守，故朕欲巡視遠俗。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, on xinhai he held court at Yanfu Hall, summoned officials of fifth rank and above, and said, "From antiquity emperors have all made inspection tours; therefore I wish to tour and observe distant customs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, on xinhai he held court at Yanfu Hall, summoned officials of fifth rank and above, and said, "From antiquity emperors have all made inspection tours; therefore I wish to tour distant regions and observe their customs.

sentences.zh: 若果為不可，何不面陳，而退有後言，何也？」

translations.literal: If it is truly impossible, why not speak face to face? Yet you withdraw and speak afterward—why?"
translations.idiomatic: If it is truly impossible, why not speak to my face? Yet you withdraw and speak behind my back—why?"

sentences.zh: 自宰相以下莫敢對。

translations.literal: From the chancellors downward, none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: From the chancellors downward, none dared reply.

sentences.zh: 詳刑大夫來公敏獨進曰：「巡守雖帝王常事，然高麗新平，餘寇尚多，西邊經略，亦未息兵。

translations.literal: Minister of Detailed Punishments Lai Gongmin alone stepped forward and said, "An inspection tour is a regular duty of emperors, yet Goguryeo has only just been pacified and remnant rebels are still numerous; campaigns on the western frontier have not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Detailed Punishments Lai Gongmin alone stepped forward and said, "An inspection tour is an ordinary duty of emperors, yet Goguryeo has only just been pacified and remnant rebels remain numerous; campaigns on the western frontier have not yet ended.

sentences.zh: 隴右戶口凋弊，鑾輿所至，供億百端，誠為未易。

translations.literal: Longyou's population is exhausted; wherever the imperial carriage goes, provisions must be supplied in countless ways—it truly would not be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou's population is exhausted; wherever the imperial carriage goes, provisions must be supplied in countless ways—it truly would not be easy.

sentences.zh: 外間實有竊議，但明制已行，故群臣不敢陳論耳。」

translations.literal: Outside there are indeed private discussions, but since the edict has already been issued, the officials dare not speak openly."
translations.idiomatic: Outside there is indeed private talk, but since the edict has already been issued, the officials dare not speak openly."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，為之罷西巡。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and canceled the western tour on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and canceled the western tour on his account.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢公敏為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long, Gongmin was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Gongmin was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，改瀚海都護府為安北都護府。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Protectorate-General of the Vast Sea was renamed Protectorate-General of the Pacified North.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the Protectorate-General of the Vast Sea was renamed Protectorate-General of the Pacified North.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑朔，詔徙吐谷渾部落就涼州南山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month, dingchou, an edict ordered the Tuyuhun tribes moved to the southern mountains of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day, dingchou, an edict ordered the Tuyuhun tribes moved to the southern mountains of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 議者恐吐蕃侵暴，使不能自存，欲先發兵擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: Those debating feared Tibetan attack would leave the tribes unable to survive, and wished to send troops first to strike Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Those debating feared Tibetan raids would leave the tribes unable to survive and wished to strike Tibet first.

sentences.zh: 右相閻立本以為去歲饑歉，未可興師。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Yan Liben held that last year's famine made raising an army impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Yan Liben argued that last year's famine made raising an army impossible.

sentences.zh: 議久不決，竟不果徙。

translations.literal: Deliberation dragged on without resolution, and in the end the move was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Debate dragged on without resolution, and in the end the move was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，大風，海溢，漂永嘉、安固六千餘家。

translations.literal: On gengyin, great winds blew and the sea overflowed, sweeping away more than 6,000 households in Yongjia and Angu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, great winds blew and the sea overflowed, sweeping away more than six thousand households in Yongjia and Angu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁巳，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，徙豫王旭輪為冀王，更名輪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Prince of Yu Xu Lun was moved to Prince of Ji and renamed Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Prince of Yu Xu Lun was reassigned as Prince of Ji and renamed Lun.

sentences.zh: 司空、太子太師、英貞武公李勣寢疾，上悉召其子弟在外者，使歸侍疾。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Duke Yingzhen the Martial Li Ji lay ill; the emperor summoned all his sons and nephews who were away to return and attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, Minister of Works, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke Yingzhen the Martial, lay ill; the emperor summoned all his sons and nephews who were away to return and attend him.

sentences.zh: 上及太子所賜藥，勣則餌之；

translations.literal: The medicine given by the emperor and crown prince, Li Ji would take;
translations.idiomatic: Medicine sent by the emperor and crown prince, Li Ji would take;

sentences.zh: 子弟為之迎醫，皆不聽進，曰：「吾本山東田夫，遭值聖明，致位三公，年將八十，豈非命邪！

translations.literal: when his sons and nephews brought physicians, he would not allow them in, saying, "I was originally a farmer of Shandong; meeting a sage and enlightened ruler, I rose to the rank of Three Dukes; I am nearing eighty—is this not fate!
translations.idiomatic: but when his sons and nephews brought physicians, he would not admit them, saying, "I was originally a farmer of Shandong; meeting a sage and enlightened ruler, I rose to the rank of Three Dukes; I am nearing eighty—is this not fate!

sentences.zh: 修短有期，豈能復就醫工求活！」

translations.literal: Length of life has its term—how could I again go to physicians to beg for life!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death have their allotted span—how could I again go to physicians to beg for life!"

sentences.zh: 一旦，忽謂其弟司衛少卿弼曰：「吾今日小愈，可共置酒為樂。」

translations.literal: One day he suddenly said to his younger brother Vice Director of the Court Guard Bi, "I am somewhat better today; let us set out wine and make merry together."
translations.idiomatic: One day he suddenly said to his younger brother Bi, vice director of the court guard, "I am somewhat better today; let us set out wine and make merry together."

sentences.zh: 於是子孫悉集，酒闌，謂弼曰：「吾自度必不起，故欲與汝曹為別耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon his descendants all gathered; when the wine was done, he said to Bi, "I consider that I shall certainly not rise again, and so wished to take leave of you all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his descendants all gathered; when the wine was done, he said to Bi, "I know I shall not rise again, and so wished to take leave of you all.

sentences.zh: 汝曹勿悲泣，聽我約束。

translations.literal: Do not weep; hear my instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Do not weep; hear my instructions.

sentences.zh: 我見房、杜平生勤苦，僅能立門戶，遭不肖子，蕩覆無餘。

translations.literal: I have seen how Fang and Du toiled all their lives and barely established their houses, yet unworthy sons brought ruin without a remnant.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen how Fang and Du toiled all their lives and barely established their houses, yet unworthy sons brought ruin without a remnant.

sentences.zh: 吾有此子孫，今悉付汝。

translations.literal: I now entrust all these descendants of mine to you.
translations.idiomatic: I now entrust all these descendants of mine to you.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，汝即遷入我堂，撫養孤幼，謹察視之。

translations.literal: When the burial is complete, move at once into my hall, nurture the orphans and young, and watch over them carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial is complete, move at once into my hall, nurture the orphans and young, and watch over them carefully.

sentences.zh: 其有志氣不倫，交遊非類者，皆先撾殺，然後以聞。」

translations.literal: Any whose ambition is unsound or who consort with unsuitable company—beat them to death first, then report it."
translations.idiomatic: Any whose ambition is unsound or who consort with unsuitable company—beat them to death first, then report it."

sentences.zh: 自是不復更言。

translations.literal: From then on he spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he spoke no more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊申，薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wushen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen, he died.

sentences.zh: 上聞之悲泣，葬日，幸未央宮，登樓望輀車慟哭。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he wept in grief; on the day of burial he visited Weiyang Palace, ascended a tower, looked upon the funeral carriage, and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he wept in grief; on the day of burial he visited Weiyang Palace, ascended a tower, looked upon the funeral carriage, and wailed.

sentences.zh: 起塚象陰山、鐵山、烏德鞬山，以旌其破突厥、薛延陀之功。

translations.literal: His tomb was built in the likeness of Yinshan, Tieshan, and Wudejianshan, to honor his achievements in breaking the Turks and Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb was built in the likeness of Yinshan, Tieshan, and Wudejianshan to honor his victories over the Turks and Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 勣為將，有謀善斷；

translations.literal: As a general, Li Ji was resourceful and good at decision;
translations.idiomatic: As a general, Li Ji was resourceful and decisive;

sentences.zh: 與人議事，從善如流。

translations.literal: when discussing affairs with others, he followed good counsel as readily as a flowing stream.
translations.idiomatic: when discussing affairs with others, he followed good counsel as readily as a flowing stream.

sentences.zh: 戰勝則歸功於下，所得金帛，悉散之將士，故人思致死，所向克捷。

translations.literal: When victorious he ascribed credit to his subordinates; gold and silk obtained he distributed entirely among his officers and soldiers, so men wished to die for him and wherever he went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: When victorious he ascribed credit to his subordinates; gold and silk obtained he distributed entirely among his officers and soldiers, so men wished to die for him and wherever he went he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 臨事選將，必訾相其狀貌豐厚者遣之。

translations.literal: When choosing generals for action, he always appraised their appearance and sent those who looked full and substantial.
translations.idiomatic: When choosing generals for action, he always appraised their appearance and sent those who looked full and substantial.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，勣曰：「薄命之人，不足與成功名。」

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Li Ji said, "Men of thin fortune are not fit to share in success and fame."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked the reason, Li Ji said, "Men of thin fortune are not fit to share in success and fame."

sentences.zh: 閨門雍睦而嚴。

translations.literal: Within his household relations were harmonious yet strict.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household relations were harmonious yet strict.

sentences.zh: 其姊嘗病，勣已為僕射，親為之煮粥。

translations.literal: When his elder sister was ill, though Li Ji was already a Grand Secretariat Director, he personally cooked porridge for her.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder sister was ill, though Li Ji was already a Grand Secretariat Director, he personally cooked porridge for her.

sentences.zh: 風回，爇其鬚鬢。

translations.literal: A gust of wind blew back and singed his beard and sideburns.
translations.idiomatic: A gust of wind blew back and singed his beard and sideburns.

sentences.zh: 姊曰：「僕妾幸多，何自苦如是！」

translations.literal: His sister said, "You have plenty of servants—why torment yourself like this!"
translations.idiomatic: His sister said, "You have plenty of servants—why torment yourself like this!"

sentences.zh: 勣曰：「非為無人使令也，顧姊老，勣亦老，雖欲久為姊煮粥，其可得乎！」

translations.literal: Li Ji said, "It is not that I have no one to order about; but my sister is old, and I too am old—though I wish I could cook porridge for you for a long time, how can that be!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji said, "It is not that I have no one to order about; but my sister is old, and I too am old—though I wish I could cook porridge for you for a long time, how can that be!"

sentences.zh: 勣常謂人：「我年十二三時為亡賴賊，逢人則殺。

translations.literal: Li Ji often told people, "When I was twelve or thirteen I was a good-for-nothing bandit and killed anyone I met.
